contraindications: Active prostate cancer — hCG-driven testosterone production directly stimulates androgen receptor-expressing prostate cancer cells; absolute contraindication; one of the most critically enforced oncological contraindications in Category VII.

Hormone receptor-positive breast cancer in men (gynecomastia-associated malignancy) — testosterone and its aromatized estradiol metabolite stimulate estrogen receptor-expressing male breast cancer cells.
Androgen-sensitive malignancies (Leydig cell tumor, certain testicular cancers) — direct LH receptor stimulation on malignant Leydig cells could accelerate tumor growth.

Primary hypogonadism with absent Leydig cell function (Klinefelter syndrome with severe testicular failure) — hCG requires functional Leydig cells to produce its effect; in subjects with no viable Leydig cells, hCG will not produce testosterone and provides no benefit.
Known hypersensitivity to hCG or urinary gonadotropin-derived formulation proteins.
Precocious puberty — LH/hCG receptor activation in children with premature puberty accelerates the condition.

Pregnancy (for uses other than medically supervised ovulation triggering) — while hCG is produced physiologically in pregnancy, exogenous administration beyond the ovulation trigger protocol must be under obstetric supervision.
Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) risk in women — in women undergoing ovarian stimulation protocols, hCG administration can trigger severe OHSS; requires clinical monitoring.
Pituitary adenoma secreting LH/FSH — in the rare context of LH/FSH-secreting pituitary tumors, adding exogenous LH mimetic stimulation is inadvisable.
sideEffects: Estrogen elevation and aromatization — the primary dose-dependent adverse effect; hCG-stimulated Leydig cell steroidogenesis produces intratesticular estradiol through aromatase activity; at doses above 500 IU serum estradiol can rise significantly; produces gynecomastia, nipple sensitivity, water retention, mood changes, and reduced libido when estrogen-to-testosterone ratio becomes unfavorable.
Water retention and edema — secondary to estrogen elevation; dose-dependent; managed with aromatase inhibitor co-administration if clinically significant.
Acne — secondary to elevated testosterone and IGF-1 activity from Leydig cell activation; dose-dependent.
Mood instability and emotional lability — from acute fluctuations in testosterone, estradiol, and their CNS effects; most pronounced in the first cycle and during high-dose protocols.
Injection site pain and bruising — standard subcutaneous injection adverse effect; mild.
Testicular hypertrophy and discomfort — from increased Leydig cell and Sertoli cell stimulation; benign; reflects pharmacological activity; more pronounced with higher doses.
Headache — uncommon; possibly from the rapid hormonal fluctuations affecting the HPG-CNS axis.

Gynecomastia — breast tissue development or enlargement from estrogen excess from Leydig cell aromatization; risk increases significantly above 1,000 IU per dose; aromatase inhibitor co-administration mitigates.
Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) in women — potentially severe and life-threatening with high-dose ovulation triggering protocols; requires clinical supervision in fertility applications.

LHCGR desensitization with continuous high-dose use — sustained supraphysiological hCG stimulation produces Leydig cell LHCGR downregulation and steroidogenic enzyme desensitization; the washout protocols are designed to prevent loss of Leydig cell sensitivity.
Benign prostatic hypertrophy worsening — testosterone elevation from hCG in men with existing BPH may worsen urinary symptoms.

records.optionName: Healthy Hair Skin and Nails Blend (HHB)
records.name: Healthy Hair Skin and Nails Blend (HHB)
records.description: The Healthy Hair Skin and Nails Blend (product code HHB) is a beauty and wellness injection built from a full panel of B-vitamins plus biotin and folic acid to support the health of hair, skin, and nails. It is a vitamin blend rather than a peptide, working through nutritional cofactor support, and given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Each milliliter contains Niacinamide 50mg, Thiamine HCl (B1) 50mg, Pantothenic Acid (B5) 25mg, Choline 10mg, Inositol 10mg, Niacin (B3) 5mg, Biotin 100mcg, Folic Acid 100mcg, and Riboflavin (B2) 100mcg. Biotin is the signature ingredient for keratin production and hair and nail strength, the B-vitamin panel supports skin health, cellular turnover, and energy metabolism, niacinamide and niacin support skin barrier function and circulation, folic acid supports cell division, and choline and inositol support general metabolic health. In practice, HHB is used by people focused on the cosmetic and structural health of their hair, skin, and nails who want injectable delivery of the key supporting vitamins rather than relying on oral supplements with variable absorption. It appeals to users experiencing brittle nails, thinning or slow-growing hair, or dull skin, and to those who simply want to support these tissues as part of a broader wellness routine. It is typically administered in the morning as a standing weekly injection, and results build gradually over weeks to months because hair and nail growth is slow and reflects cofactor availability over time. Unlike the fat-loss blends, this is a wellness and appearance-focused formula rather than a body-composition tool. Mechanistically, HHB supplies the B-vitamin cofactors that keratin synthesis, skin cell turnover, and energy metabolism depend on, with biotin as the central ingredient for hair and nail structure and the broader panel supporting the metabolic and circulatory environment that healthy tissue needs. Users should set realistic timelines: because hair and nails grow slowly, visible improvements typically take one to three months of consistent use. B-vitamins are water soluble and generally well tolerated, with excess amounts excreted, though niacin can cause a temporary flushing sensation. Injection sites should be rotated, and anyone who is pregnant, has kidney disease, or is on medication that interacts with folate should consult a physician first.

rows.notes: Direct-dose beauty and wellness vitamin injection with no titration required. A typical protocol is 0.5 to 1 mL administered subcutaneously or intramuscularly 1 to 2 times per week, in the morning. Allow one to three months of consistent use for visible hair, skin, and nail improvements. Rotate injection sites. Suitable for continuous use.

contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to any B-vitamin, biotin, folic acid, or formulation excipient.
Pregnancy or breastfeeding unless directed and supervised by a physician.
Active kidney disease unless medically supervised.
Note that high biotin intake can interfere with certain lab tests, including thyroid and cardiac troponin assays, so inform your provider before bloodwork.
sideEffects: Temporary flushing or warmth from the niacin content.
Injection site irritation, redness, warmth, or tenderness.
Bright yellow urine from riboflavin, which is harmless.
Transient acne or skin breakouts in sensitive individuals.
Mild gastrointestinal upset.
Interference with biotin-based laboratory tests.

records.name: Hexarelin
records.description: Hexarelin (also known as examorelin) is the most potent GHRP ever synthesized — a hexapeptide that produces the largest acute GH pulses of any compound in the GHRP class, estimated to generate GH release 2–3 times greater than native GHRH alone at equivalent molar doses. It activates GHS-R1a (the ghrelin receptor) on pituitary somatotrophs with particularly high affinity, simultaneously suppressing hypothalamic somatostatin (the GH-inhibiting hormone) to amplify the net GH output further. Unlike ipamorelin or GHRP-2, hexarelin has no selectivity for the GH response over other GHS-R1a-mediated effects — it elevates cortisol and prolactin significantly with every injection, placing it in the same non-selective category as GHRP-6, but with even greater potency across all pathways. What makes hexarelin uniquely interesting beyond its GH-releasing properties is its secondary mechanism: it binds directly to CD36 scavenger receptors on cardiomyocytes, independent of the GH pathway, producing cardioprotective effects including protection from ischemia-reperfusion injury, reduction in reactive oxygen species, and decreased apoptosis in cardiac cells. This CD36-mediated cardiac benefit is not shared by other GHRPs. The single most clinically important limitation of hexarelin is rapid receptor desensitization. GHS-R1a downregulation begins within 2–4 weeks of continuous daily use, producing progressively diminishing GH responses even at escalating doses. This is called tachyphylaxis, and hexarelin is more prone to it than any other GHRP. Unlike GHRP-2 or ipamorelin where cycles of 8–12 weeks are practical, hexarelin cycles are limited to a strict maximum of 4–8 weeks, after which a full equal-length washout (4 weeks minimum) is required for receptor sensitivity to recover. This desensitization is the primary reason hexarelin has been largely replaced by ipamorelin for routine GH optimization protocols — ipamorelin delivers a clean, sustainable GH pulse across a 12–16 week cycle without tachyphylaxis. Research protocols that specifically leverage hexarelin tend to fall into two categories: short-duration maximum GH output bursts (4–6 weeks at maximum dose before a break) and cardiac-focused protocols targeting CD36-mediated cardioprotection. The cardioprotective effect has been demonstrated in isolated human cardiac tissue studies and multiple animal models of cardiac ischemia, making it a legitimate research target for subjects with cardiovascular risk or recovering from cardiac events — though clinical human trial data for this indication remains limited. Given its non-selective profile, hexarelin is best reserved for experienced researchers who have established their baseline tolerance to GHRPs via ipamorelin or GHRP-2 first.

rows.notes: Must be used for very short durations due to rapid desensitization.

washout: Cycle Length: Maximum 4 weeks.
Washout: Must be followed by equal time off (4 weeks) to restore receptor sensitivity.

History of prolactinoma or clinically elevated prolactin — hexarelin produces the most significant prolactin elevation of any GHRP.
Gynecomastia or active breast tissue concerns in men — prolactin elevation significantly increases risk.
High baseline cortisol, Cushing's syndrome, or adrenal hyperactivity — hexarelin produces the most pronounced cortisol elevation of any GHRP; additive HPA axis load.
Anxiety disorders — cortisol elevation amplifies anxiety.
Uncontrolled diabetes mellitus or severe insulin resistance.
Diabetic ketoacidosis.
History of pituitary adenoma or disruption of the pituitary axis.
Mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS) or histamine sensitivity — hexarelin may trigger histamine release.
Pregnancy — safety not established.
Breastfeeding — safety not established.
Known hypersensitivity to hexarelin or excipients.
Concomitant glucocorticoid therapy — blunts GH response and compounds cumulative cortisol load.
Concurrent use with other GHRPs (ipamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6) — receptor competition without additive benefit.
Concurrent use with HGH 191aa — additive GH axis overstimulation.
Subjects intending long-term GH optimization protocols — rapid desensitization makes hexarelin unsuitable for cycles beyond 4–8 weeks; use ipamorelin for long-term use.
sideEffects: Rapid receptor desensitization (tachyphylaxis) — the defining limitation of hexarelin; GH response begins attenuating within 2–4 weeks of daily use and progresses with continued administration; requires full washout to recover.
Significant cortisol elevation — the most pronounced cortisol increase among all GHRPs; through direct GHS-R1a activation in adrenocortical cells; chronic use may lead to cumulative HPA axis burden.
Significant prolactin elevation — via GHS-R1a on pituitary lactotrophs; chronic elevation increases gynecomastia risk in men and may cause menstrual irregularities.

Water retention and bloating — high-amplitude GH pulses drive more pronounced fluid retention than lower-potency GHRPs.
Appetite stimulation — moderate; begins 15–30 minutes post-injection; more manageable than GHRP-6 but more than ipamorelin.
Fatigue and drowsiness — lethargy following the GH pulse.
Head rush and flushing — transient vasodilation from the GH pulse.
Tingling or numbness in extremities.

Injection site redness and swelling.

Joint stiffness — GH-mediated periarticular fluid.
Elevated IGF-1 — monitor with blood work; supraphysiologic IGF-1 levels possible at high doses.

records.name: HGH 191AA (Somatropin)
records.description: HGH 191AA (somatropin) is bio-identical human growth hormone — a 191 amino acid single-chain polypeptide with a molecular weight of approximately 22 kDa, structurally identical to the growth hormone produced by the anterior pituitary gland. The "191AA" designation distinguishes it from obsolete 192AA formulations (which contained an extra methionine residue that increased immunogenicity) and confirms structural identity with endogenous GH. Unlike all GH secretagogues in this database (CJC-1295, ipamorelin, GHRP-2, sermorelin, etc.) which stimulate the pituitary to produce more of its own GH, HGH 191AA directly replaces or supplements endogenous GH without requiring pituitary participation. It binds directly to GH receptors in the liver, adipose tissue, muscle, and bone to produce its downstream effects, including the stimulation of IGF-1 production from the liver — the primary mediator of most of HGH's anabolic effects. The pharmacological profile of exogenous HGH is broad and well-documented: it drives lipolysis (fat breakdown) in peripheral adipose tissue, promotes lean mass retention and protein synthesis via IGF-1, increases bone mineral density, improves skin collagen synthesis and elasticity, enhances immune function, and accelerates soft tissue repair. Unlike secretagogues that preserve pituitary pulsatility, exogenous HGH creates predictable pharmacokinetic curves based on the injection timing — morning fasted injections produce a GH peak that mimics the natural early-morning pulse, while pre-bed injections align with the nocturnal GH surge. At therapeutic doses (1–4 IU daily), the effects accumulate over months of consistent administration, making HGH a long-cycle compound by design. HGH 191AA occupies a category-above relationship with all secretagogues in this database. Secretagogues (CJC-1295, ipamorelin, sermorelin, tesamorelin) stimulate the pituitary to release whatever GH it can produce — effective for younger subjects with healthy pituitary function, but limited by pituitary capacity. HGH 191AA bypasses the pituitary entirely, delivering exogenous GH directly and producing GH and IGF-1 levels that secretagogues cannot match at their standard doses. This is both its advantage (higher ceiling, predictable dose-response) and its risk profile escalation: exogenous GH suppresses endogenous GH production during the cycle, requiring a gradual taper upon cessation to allow pituitary function to recover. It is contraindicated with all secretagogues — adding CJC-1295 or ipamorelin to an HGH protocol is redundant stimulation of a pituitary that is already being bypassed.

Paresthesia (tingling/numbness) — in hands and feet; from GH-related fluid pressure on peripheral nerves.

Peripheral swelling (hands, feet, face) — edema, particularly in the first weeks.
