records.name: Pancragen
records.description: Pancragen is a synthetic tetrapeptide (Lys-Glu-Asp-Pro) Khavinson bioregulator derived from pancreatic tissue polypeptide extracts — identified as the bioactive core sequence responsible for the insulin-regulatory, beta-cell protective, and pancreatic exocrine/endocrine normalization activity of the native pancreatic extract. The pancreas contains two functionally distinct compartments that Pancragen addresses through its organ-specific bioregulator mechanism: the endocrine pancreas (islets of Langerhans), which contains the beta cells that produce insulin, alpha cells that produce glucagon, delta cells that produce somatostatin, and PP cells that produce pancreatic polypeptide — all coordinating glucose homeostasis; and the exocrine pancreas, which produces the digestive enzymes (lipase, amylase, protease) delivered to the duodenum. Pancreatic aging involves progressive decline in both compartments: beta cell mass decreases with age, insulin secretory response to glucose challenge diminishes (particularly the critical first-phase insulin release that clamps post-prandial glucose spikes), beta cell oxidative stress and ER stress accumulate, exocrine enzyme production declines, and pancreatic duct epithelial cell regeneration capacity diminishes. Pancragen acts as a bioregulator at the pancreatic cellular level — interacting with islet cell and exocrine cell surface receptors and transcription factors to normalize the gene expression programs governing insulin synthesis and secretion, beta cell survival, glucose sensing machinery (GLUT2 expression, glucokinase activity), and exocrine enzyme production. This upstream transcriptional normalization produces the insulin regulation improvements observed in Pancragen research without the pharmacological insulin secretion forcing that characterizes sulfonylureas and other insulin secretagogues. The metabolic context of Pancragen's application in this database is best understood in relation to the GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide, tirzepatide, retatrutide) that occupy Category I. GLP-1 agonists address glucose metabolism primarily through peripheral mechanisms — slowing gastric emptying, reducing glucagon, and amplifying the GLP-1/GIP incretin response to meals to force higher insulin output. Pancragen works upstream at the pancreatic tissue level: instead of pharmacologically amplifying the insulin secretory response to each meal (as GLP-1 agonists do), Pancragen seeks to normalize the quality and responsiveness of the beta cell itself — restoring the gene regulatory programs governing glucose sensing accuracy, first-phase insulin kinetics, and beta cell resilience against oxidative stress. The synergy designations with semaglutide and tirzepatide reflect complementary mechanisms: GLP-1/GIP agonists maximize the insulin secretory signal from each meal stimulus while Pancragen simultaneously normalizes the quality and health of the beta cells being stimulated. The two approaches address the output signal (GLP-1 agonists) and the sending tissue health (Pancragen) of the insulin secretory process simultaneously. The practical relevance is greatest in subjects with prediabetes, metabolic syndrome, or early-stage T2DM where beta cell function is declining but not yet exhausted. The contraindication with insulin-dependent Type 1 diabetes management requires specific context. In T1DM, the autoimmune destruction of beta cells means that exogenous insulin replacement is the non-negotiable treatment foundation. Pancragen's bioregulator activity targeting pancreatic tissue gene programs could theoretically have unpredictable interactions with residual beta cell function, insulin requirements, or the autoimmune process in T1DM — making unsupervised use inadvisable. The hypoglycemia risk in subjects on insulin or sulfonylureas reflects the additive insulin sensitization: if Pancragen improves beta cell glucose responsiveness while exogenous insulin or sulfonylureas are already driving insulin levels, the combined effect could lower blood glucose below safe thresholds. Blood glucose monitoring during the first cycle in medicated diabetic subjects is the essential safety precaution.

records.name: PE-22-28
records.description: PE-22-28 is a synthetic peptide fragment corresponding to residues 22–28 of spadin — itself a naturally occurring peptide shed from the propeptide region of NTSR3/sortilin, a neurotensin receptor family member. The identification of PE-22-28 emerged from the discovery that spadin acts as an endogenous antagonist of the TREK-1 potassium channel, and that TREK-1 blockade produces rapid antidepressant effects in rodent models. TREK-1 (TWIK-related K+ channel 1, encoded by KCNK2) is a two-pore domain background potassium channel that sets the resting membrane potential of neurons and whose activity is increased under conditions of cellular stress, membrane stretch, anesthetics, fatty acids, and the lipid signaling molecule lysophosphatidylcholine. Hyperactivation of TREK-1 hyperpolarizes neurons — silencing them — and is mechanistically associated with depressive states. TREK-1 knockout mice display a constitutively antidepressant-resistant-to-stress phenotype with elevated serotonin and norepinephrine in synaptic clefts, establishing the channel as a bona fide antidepressant target. PE-22-28 is the optimized fragment of spadin with the highest potency-to-stability ratio for TREK-1 antagonism, blocking the channel's open state and allowing neuronal membrane potential to return to a more depolarized, excitable resting state — effectively disinhibiting serotonergic and noradrenergic neurons in the raphe nuclei and locus coeruleus that are suppressed in depression. The antidepressant mechanism of PE-22-28 is mechanistically orthogonal to every other antidepressant class in clinical use. SSRIs block serotonin reuptake transporters (SERT) to increase synaptic serotonin half-life. SNRIs block both SERT and NET (norepinephrine transporter). TCAs block multiple reuptake transporters and receptors. MAOIs block the degradation enzyme for monoamines. Ketamine blocks NMDA receptors. PE-22-28 does none of these — it acts upstream by removing the potassium channel hyperpolarization brake on the neurons that produce serotonin and norepinephrine, allowing them to fire more freely and release neurotransmitter tonically rather than pharmacologically forcing transmitter accumulation in the synapse. This mechanism predicts — and the research data confirms — that PE-22-28 onset of action is rapid (within hours to days, not weeks), that it does not produce the sexual dysfunction, emotional blunting, weight gain, or withdrawal syndrome associated with SSRI/SNRI use, and that its antidepressant activity is not dependent on chronic serotonin receptor downregulation (the proposed mechanism underlying the 4–6 week SSRI delay). The synergy with Selank is mechanistically complementary: PE-22-28 restores tonic monoamine neurotransmitter availability by disinhibiting raphe/LC neurons via TREK-1 blockade, while Selank reduces the amygdalar anxiety and hyperarousal that co-presents with and worsens depression — addressing the two dominant neurobiological components of mixed anxiety-depression from independent mechanisms. PE-22-28 represents the most mechanistically novel antidepressant compound in this database and among the most novel in the entire neuropeptide research space. The human clinical data is limited — Phase 1 and early Phase 2 trials are the current state — and all efficacy conclusions derive from preclinical models and early clinical observation. The "Neural Stimulant" property tag reflects the net neuronal excitability increase from TREK-1 antagonism, which produces the stimulant-adjacent side effects (overstimulation, headache) at higher doses and confirms the morning dosing requirement. The bipolar disorder contraindication is among the most important in Category V: TREK-1 antagonism increases neuronal excitability and monoamine tone in a manner that, in subjects with bipolar vulnerability, could trigger manic switch — the same risk that warrants caution with antidepressants as monotherapy in bipolar disorder.

records.name: Peg MGF (Pegylated Mechano Growth Factor)
records.description: Peg-MGF (Pegylated Mechano Growth Factor) is the extended half-life version of MGF, produced by attaching polyethylene glycol (PEG) chains to the MGF peptide backbone — the same pegylation technology used to extend the half-life of pharmaceutical biologics. In its native form, MGF is degraded within 5–7 minutes in the bloodstream by the rapid cleavage of its C-terminal E-domain. Pegylation shields the peptide from enzymatic degradation, extending the functional half-life to approximately 48 hours. This single pharmacokinetic change transforms MGF from a locally acting, immediately post-workout tool into a systemically distributed, subcutaneously injectable compound that circulates and activates satellite cells throughout the body — not just in the injected muscle. The extended half-life fundamentally changes the administration logic. Because Peg-MGF circulates for ~48 hours, it does not need to be injected bilaterally into the trained muscle group — subcutaneous injection in the abdomen delivers systemic satellite cell activation across all muscle tissues. This makes it suitable for rest-day administration: injecting on recovery days allows the 48-hour circulation window to overlap with the period when muscle repair and remodeling are most active (24–72 hours post-training). Some researchers use a split approach: MGF (non-peg) bilaterally IM immediately post-workout for acute local satellite cell activation, followed by Peg-MGF on rest days for systemic continued activation. This theoretically covers both the acute local signal and the sustained systemic signal. The trade-off for the extended half-life is reduced localized specificity. Where native MGF's short half-life concentrates activity precisely in the injected tissue, Peg-MGF's systemic distribution activates satellite cells broadly — which is advantageous for full-body training protocols but less precise for single muscle group targeting. Hypoglycemia risk persists via the same IGF-1 receptor mechanism as native MGF, though it is more diffuse and gradual rather than the acute post-injection dip seen with non-pegylated forms. Blood glucose monitoring is advised, particularly when stacking Peg-MGF with IGF-1 LR3 or GH axis compounds.

records.name: Pinealon
records.description: Pinealon is a synthetic tripeptide (Glu-Asp-Arg) Khavinson bioregulator derived from pineal gland and broader CNS tissue polypeptide extracts — identified as the bioactive sequence responsible for the neuroprotective, antioxidant, and central nervous system regulatory activity of the CNS-derived extract fraction. Despite being named for the pineal gland, Pinealon's mechanism of action spans the entire CNS: it acts as a pan-neuronal bioregulator targeting multiple CNS cell types simultaneously — neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and microglia — normalizing the gene expression programs governing cellular oxidative defense, mitochondrial function, neurotrophic factor production, and the inflammatory phenotype of CNS tissue. The primary mechanistic emphasis of Pinealon is antioxidant protection: the CNS is disproportionately vulnerable to oxidative stress due to its high metabolic rate (20% of total body oxygen consumption in 2% of total body mass), high polyunsaturated fatty acid content in neuronal membranes (highly susceptible to lipid peroxidation), relatively limited catalase and glutathione activity compared to peripheral tissues, and the iron concentration in basal ganglia and substantia nigra that catalyzes hydroxyl radical generation via the Fenton reaction. Pinealon normalizes the expression of endogenous antioxidant enzymes (superoxide dismutase, glutathione peroxidase, catalase) and reduces the oxidative DNA damage and mitochondrial dysfunction that accumulate in CNS tissue with aging — providing the biochemical foundation for the cognitive, neuroprotective, and neurological function improvements observed in Pinealon research. The research evidence for Pinealon spans both healthy aging cognitive decline and acute neurological injury contexts. In aging subjects, Pinealon administration produced improvements in cognitive test performance (memory, attention, processing speed), normalization of EEG activity parameters toward younger adult patterns, reduction in CSF and serum markers of oxidative neural injury, and improvements in cerebrovascular function through the endothelial-neural interface. In the neurological injury context, Pinealon demonstrated the ability to reduce ischemia-reperfusion-related neuronal death in animal models of stroke, improve post-ischemic functional recovery, and attenuate the excitotoxic cascade that mediates secondary neuronal damage following acute brain injury. The circadian biology connection to Pinealon's morning dosing is important: the pineal gland operates on a strict light-dark circadian schedule, with maximal melatonin synthesis occurring during darkness. Pinealon's interaction with pineal and CNS circadian gene programs means morning administration — when the pineal is in its lowest activity phase — provides the bioregulator stimulus at the point where normalization of the circadian neural program produces the greatest downstream effect on daytime CNS function and the subsequent night's melatonin rhythm. The distinction between Pinealon and Cortagen — the two CNS-targeted Khavinson bioregulators — is one of specificity versus breadth. Cortagen is a cortex-specific bioregulator targeting the cortical neuron and synaptic plasticity programs that govern higher cognitive function. Pinealon is a pan-CNS bioregulator with primary emphasis on oxidative defense, mitochondrial function, and CNS circadian regulation — acting across all CNS regions rather than specifically at the cortical level. Their synergistic designation reflects the complementary scope: Cortagen provides the cortex-specific neuroplasticity and neurotrophic support, while Pinealon provides the CNS-wide oxidative defense infrastructure that protects all neurons including the cortical ones Cortagen supports. Their combination addresses both the quality of cortical neuronal function (Cortagen) and the survival infrastructure protecting those neurons from oxidative and mitochondrial damage (Pinealon) — a mechanistically logical and well-characterized synergy.

records.name: PNC-27
records.description: PNC-27 is a synthetic anticancer peptide engineered by Matthew Pincus and colleagues at SUNY Downstate Medical Center, constructed from two functional domains fused into a single molecule: a p53 activation domain sequence (residues 12–26 of the p53 transactivation domain) linked to a penetratin cell-membrane-penetrating sequence (from the Antennapedia homeodomain). The design premise is mechanistically elegant: cancer cells, unlike normal cells, aberrantly overexpress MDM-2 (murine double minute 2, known as HDM-2 in humans) on their plasma membrane — MDM-2 is normally a nuclear/cytoplasmic E3 ubiquitin ligase that targets p53 for proteasomal degradation, but in the malignant phenotype it is trafficked to the cell surface membrane where it becomes a distinguishing molecular marker of cancer cell membranes that is essentially absent from normal cell surfaces. PNC-27 is designed to bind this membrane-expressed HDM-2 with high affinity through its p53-derived sequence (the natural binding partner of MDM-2), and then use the penetratin sequence to insert into and disrupt the cancer cell's plasma membrane lipid bilayer — physically puncturing the membrane in a manner that produces necrosis rather than apoptosis. This membrane disruption mechanism is distinct from FOXO4-DRI's pro-apoptotic mechanism: PNC-27 does not require intracellular signaling, receptor internalization, or functional downstream apoptotic machinery — it directly destroys the physical integrity of the cancer cell membrane at the HDM-2 binding site, producing immediate cell death through osmotic lysis and membrane fragmentation. The cancer cell selectivity of PNC-27 is predicated entirely on the differential membrane expression of HDM-2: normal cells do not express HDM-2 on their plasma membrane in meaningful quantities, providing the therapeutic window that makes PNC-27 preferentially cytotoxic to cancer cells over normal tissue. In vitro data demonstrates PNC-27 killing activity against pancreatic cancer, breast cancer, leukemia, lung cancer, melanoma, and other HDM-2-overexpressing tumor cell lines while sparing normal cell lines expressing minimal membrane HDM-2. The membrane disruption mechanism produces cell death by necrosis — a fundamentally different cell death pathway than apoptosis — which has implications for the immune response: necrotic cell death releases intracellular contents (DAMPs — damage-associated molecular patterns) that activate innate immune pattern recognition and can trigger anti-tumor immune responses. This is the mechanistic basis for the synergy designation with Thymosin Alpha-1: PNC-27 kills cancer cells and releases tumor antigens through necrosis; Thymosin Alpha-1 simultaneously activates T-cell-mediated adaptive immunity, MHC-I expression, and dendritic cell maturation — creating a coordinated innate kill + adaptive immune amplification combination that could theoretically produce systemic anti-tumor responses beyond the local PNC-27 killing effect. The category designation as strictly experimental oncology research compound reflects the clinical development status of PNC-27 accurately. The compound has not progressed through Phase 3 clinical trials; the evidence base is primarily in vitro and limited animal data with early phase human clinical observation. The titration protocol (1–3mg/day with the alternative 20-week escalation to 1,000mcg) reflects research use experience rather than established clinical dosing. The absence of well-characterized contraindications for healthy subjects reflects the intended exclusive use context: PNC-27 is not a wellness or longevity peptide — it is an experimental oncology compound whose use in the absence of malignancy has no established therapeutic rationale, and whose safety profile in non-cancer subjects (who lack the HDM-2 membrane overexpression that provides selectivity) has not been characterized. Normal cells with any degree of stress-induced surface HDM-2 expression could theoretically be at risk from PNC-27 exposure — the selectivity window is narrower and less predictable in non-malignant subjects.

records.name: Prostamax
records.description: Prostamax is a synthetic tetrapeptide (Lys-Glu-Asp-Trp) Khavinson bioregulator derived from prostate gland tissue polypeptide extracts — identified as the bioactive core sequence responsible for the prostate epithelial cell regulatory, anti-inflammatory, and tissue-normalizing activity of the native prostatic extract. The prostate is a walnut-sized glandular organ in the male pelvis that produces the fluid components of semen, including citric acid, zinc, proteolytic enzymes (PSA/kallikrein-3), and seminal plasma proteins that constitute approximately 30% of ejaculate volume. The glandular and stromal architecture of the prostate is regulated by a complex androgen-dependent and growth factor-dependent tissue homeostasis involving prostatic epithelial cells, prostatic stromal fibroblasts, and smooth muscle cells. Prostate aging involves two primary pathological trajectories: benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), characterized by non-malignant stromal and epithelial cell proliferation that enlarges the prostate and compresses the urethra producing lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS); and prostatic inflammation (prostatitis), characterized by inflammatory cell infiltration, cytokine-driven stromal remodeling, and the chronic pelvic pain, voiding dysfunction, and sexual function impairment that accompany it. Prostamax acts as a bioregulator at the prostatic epithelial cell and stromal cell level — interacting with prostate-specific cell surface receptors and transcription factors to normalize the gene expression programs governing cell proliferation control, inflammatory cytokine production, androgen receptor sensitivity, and the growth factor signaling (EGF, FGF, IGF-1) that regulates prostatic tissue homeostasis. This upstream transcriptional normalization approach is mechanistically distinct from standard BPH pharmacotherapy (5-alpha reductase inhibitors reduce dihydrotestosterone; alpha-blockers relax prostatic smooth muscle) — Prostamax targets the cellular gene regulatory machinery underlying the BPH process rather than its hormonal or mechanical downstream consequences. The Khavinson research on Prostamax and its predecessors (bovine prostate-derived polypeptide extracts) spans clinical series in men with BPH and chronic prostatitis. Documented effects include: reduction in prostate volume measurements by transrectal ultrasound over treatment cycles, improvement in urinary flow parameters (peak flow rate, post-void residual volume), reduction in the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) — the validated questionnaire measuring LUTS severity, improvement in the quality-of-life domain of prostate symptom assessment, and in chronic prostatitis series, reduction in pelvic pain scores and improvement in sexual function metrics including ejaculatory function. The synergy designation with Testagen is mechanistically grounded in the functional relationship between the prostate and testicular androgen production: the prostate is the primary androgen-responsive peripheral organ, and its health is directly linked to testicular Leydig cell function and testosterone production quality. Testagen addresses the testicular gene programs governing testosterone synthesis; Prostamax addresses the prostatic epithelial programs governing how that testosterone signal is processed and how the prostate tissue maintains homeostasis in response to it. Together they address both ends of the androgen production-response axis simultaneously. The cancer safety dimension of Prostamax deserves specific attention given the prostate's status as the most common non-skin cancer site in aging men. Prostamax's gene program normalization mechanism includes normalization of cell proliferation control — moving dysregulated proliferative gene programs back toward the homeostatic balance of younger prostatic tissue. This mechanism is the basis of the BPH benefit and is theoretically anti-proliferative in the context of benign hyperplasia. However, in the context of existing prostate cancer, normalization of prostatic cell gene programs in tissue containing malignant clones is an unknown intervention: Prostamax has not been evaluated in prostate cancer tissue, and whether its bioregulator activity on prostatic cells affects malignant vs. benign cells differentially is not established. PSA monitoring before and during Prostamax cycles is appropriate in subjects over 50 with elevated baseline PSA or family history of prostate cancer.

records.name: PT-141 (Bremelanotide)
records.description: PT-141 (Bremelanotide) is a synthetic cyclic heptapeptide melanocortin receptor agonist derived from Melanotan II, developed specifically to retain the central sexual arousal activity of MT-II while eliminating the tanning activity. It is the first and only FDA-approved melanocortin-based treatment for hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) in premenopausal women (approved 2019 as Vyleesi), and the first approved pharmacological agent that acts centrally — directly on the brain — rather than peripherally to produce sexual arousal. PT-141's mechanism is fundamentally different from phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil): those drugs act peripherally on penile vasculature to facilitate erection by blocking cGMP degradation, requiring sexual arousal to already be present; PT-141 acts on MC4R and MC3R receptors in the hypothalamus and limbic system to generate the central neurological state of sexual desire itself. The specific hypothalamic circuits activated by MC4R agonism include the medial preoptic area (MPOA) and paraventricular nucleus (PVN) — regions that govern sexual motivation, arousal, and the initiation of copulatory behavior in mammalian neuroscience. This central mechanism produces sexual desire that is not contingent on visual or physical stimulation, which is why PT-141 is effective in both psychological and physiological low-libido presentations. The clinical development history of PT-141 and the pharmacological distinction between its approved and research uses are important context. In Phase 3 trials for HSDD in women, bremelanotide demonstrated statistically significant improvements in satisfying sexual events and desire scores versus placebo, establishing the central melanocortin pathway as a legitimate pharmaceutical target for sexual dysfunction. In male subjects, PT-141 has demonstrated efficacy for erectile dysfunction including cases refractory to PDE5 inhibitors — a critically important subset, since approximately 30–40% of men with ED do not respond adequately to sildenafil or tadalafil, and PT-141's central mechanism provides a complementary or alternative pathway. The synergy between PT-141 and PDE5 inhibitors is mechanistically logical: PT-141 provides the central neurological arousal signal while PDE5 inhibitors amplify the peripheral vascular response — addressing both the CNS initiation and the penile vascular execution components of erection simultaneously. The 4–6 hour lead time before the desired effect is the most practically important dosing consideration — unlike PDE5 inhibitors (onset 30–60 minutes), PT-141's hypothalamic circuit activation requires significantly more time to translate into subjective arousal. The nausea that is PT-141's primary and most impactful side effect is mechanistically inseparable from its efficacy at the doses required for full sexual arousal response. MC4R receptors in the area postrema (the brain's chemoreceptor trigger zone) are activated alongside the hypothalamic arousal receptors — activating a nausea-emesis circuit as a direct pharmacological consequence of the same receptor agonism that drives arousal. This is not an idiosyncratic adverse reaction; it is a predictable MC4R-mediated effect that occurs in the majority of subjects at doses of 1.75mg and above. The micro-dosing protocol (500mcg) was developed specifically to find the floor dose that produces meaningful arousal benefit with tolerable nausea — the trade-off being reduced arousal intensity in exchange for side effect manageability. The 16-week daily low-dose protocol operates on a different premise: sustained sub-threshold MC4R stimulation producing cumulative libido improvement rather than acute arousal events, with the daily 500–1500mcg range chosen to remain below the acute nausea threshold while delivering tonic melanocortin system support.

rows.notes: Administer 4 to 6 hours BEFORE desired effect.

contraindications: Uncontrolled hypertension — PT-141 produces transient blood pressure increases (both systolic and diastolic) lasting 8–12 hours post-injection via MC4R-mediated sympathetic activation; in subjects with uncontrolled high blood pressure this cardiovascular effect represents meaningful added risk.

Severe or unstable cardiovascular disease (recent MI, unstable angina, significant arrhythmia) — the transient BP elevation and sympathetic activation from MC4R agonism is contraindicated in subjects with marginal cardiovascular reserve.

History of significant orthostatic hypotension — PT-141 can produce transient hypotension in some subjects as the MC3R vasodilatory component briefly predominates; combined with orthostatic instability this creates fall and syncope risk.

Concurrent use with PDE5 inhibitors in subjects with cardiovascular disease — while the PT-141/PDE5 inhibitor combination is used in research, in subjects with significant cardiovascular disease the additive vasodilatory and hemodynamic effects require medical supervision.
Concurrent use with antihypertensive medications — MC4R-mediated sympathetic effects of PT-141 may transiently override antihypertensive therapy and produce unpredictable blood pressure excursions.
Known hypersensitivity to PT-141, bremelanotide, or melanocortin-derived peptides.
Pregnancy — MC4R agonism has effects on HPA axis and hypothalamic function not established as safe during pregnancy.
Breastfeeding — no safety data.
Active psychiatric conditions requiring mood stabilizers or antipsychotics — MC4R agonism affects dopaminergic tone in limbic circuits that overlap with the targets of these medications.

History of priapism or predisposition to prolonged erection (sickle cell trait, multiple myeloma, leukemia) — PT-141's central arousal mechanism can trigger prolonged erections in predisposed subjects.
sideEffects: Nausea — the primary, most common, and most clinically impactful adverse effect; occurs in the majority of subjects at doses of 1.0mg and above; caused by MC4R activation in the area postrema (chemoreceptor trigger zone); onset within 30–60 minutes of injection; duration typically 1–4 hours; managed by microdosing (500mcg) or prophylactic antiemetics.
Flushing — facial and upper body flushing from MC3R/MC4R-mediated cutaneous vasodilation; immediate onset; typically lasts 1–2 hours; more pronounced at higher doses.

Transient blood pressure increase — systolic BP elevation of 6–8 mmHg and diastolic 4–6 mmHg documented in clinical trials; onset within 30 minutes; duration 8–12 hours; the primary cardiovascular safety concern.
Headache — common; related to the transient blood pressure changes and MC4R-mediated cerebrovascular effects; typically resolves within 1–2 hours.

Priapism (prolonged erection) — rare but serious; unresolved erections lasting more than 4 hours require emergency medical intervention to prevent ischemic penile damage; more likely at higher doses or in predisposed subjects.
Spontaneous erections — MC4R activation in the hypothalamus produces erections independent of sexual stimulation; a desired effect in the ED indication but problematic in the wrong context.
Fatigue and lethargy — post-arousal effect as the acute MC4R activation wave resolves; typically 2–4 hours after peak effect.
Yawning — a distinctive and frequently reported MC4R activation marker; not pathological but a reliable signal of PT-141 activity onset.

MC4R desensitization with frequent use — the rationale for the 2-dose-per-week maximum; high-frequency MC4R agonism produces receptor downregulation and tachyphylaxis; the 16-week daily protocol's lower doses mitigate this but the 8-week washout is required.
Transient skin hyperpigmentation — MC1R is activated to a lesser degree than in Melanotan I/II but some subjects note mild transient darkening of moles or skin tone with repeated use.
Injection site reactions — mild bruising, erythema, and soreness at the subcutaneous site.

records.name: Recomp Prime
records.description: Recomp Prime is a body recomposition and metabolic optimization blend combining Tesamorelin, Ipamorelin, AOD-9604, and MOTS-c into a single coordinated fat-loss and GH-axis support platform. The blend is structured around a 2mg Tesamorelin, 3mg Ipamorelin, 5mg AOD-9604, and 5mg MOTS-c ratio, creating a 15mg total vial with a 2:3:5:5 composition. Tesamorelin provides GHRH-driven pituitary GH pulsatility, while Ipamorelin complements it through GHS-R1a activation, creating dual-pathway GH secretagogue support. AOD-9604 contributes the lipolytic fragment of HGH, targeting fat-mobilization signaling without functioning as full growth hormone. MOTS-c provides the mitochondrial and metabolic layer through AMPK signaling, supporting glucose handling, fatty acid oxidation, and metabolic flexibility. From a performance and optimization standpoint, Recomp Prime is positioned for visceral adiposity, abdominal fat accumulation, body recomposition, metabolic syndrome with impaired mitochondrial output, age-related GH-axis decline, and post-steroid body composition restoration. The blend is subcutaneous only because all four components require systemic receptor access across pituitary, adipocyte, GH-axis, and cellular metabolic pathways. It is not an intranasal blend. Recomp Prime is best suited for structured cycles built around fasted morning administration, where GH-axis signaling, lipolysis, and AMPK-driven mitochondrial utilization can be aligned with training, nutrition, and fat-loss programming.

records.name: Relaxation PM (RP226)
records.description: Relaxation PM (product code RP226) is an evening recovery and sleep-support injection built from calming amino acids and melatonin. It is a vitamin and amino blend rather than a peptide, working through neurotransmitter support and circadian signaling, and given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Each milliliter contains GABA 100mg, Melatonin 1mg, Arginine 100mg, and Glutamine 25mg. GABA is the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter and supports a calm, relaxed state, melatonin is the hormone that signals the onset of sleep and helps regulate the circadian rhythm, arginine supports growth hormone release during sleep and improves blood flow, and glutamine supports recovery, immune function, and gut health. In practice, Relaxation PM is used by people who want support for sleep quality, evening relaxation, and overnight recovery, making it the counterpart to the energizing daytime blends in this category. It is administered before bed rather than in the morning, and appeals to users whose training and fat-loss efforts are being undermined by poor sleep or high stress. The combination of GABA and melatonin targets the wind-down and sleep-onset process, while the arginine and glutamine support the body recovery processes that happen overnight, particularly the natural growth hormone pulse during deep sleep. It is commonly used by hard-training individuals who want to maximize recovery and by anyone looking for a non-prescription evening relaxation aid. Mechanistically, RP226 combines inhibitory neurotransmitter support (GABA) with circadian sleep signaling (melatonin) and overnight anabolic and recovery support (arginine driving nocturnal growth hormone release, glutamine supporting tissue repair and immunity). The result is a blend intended to help users fall asleep, stay relaxed, and recover more fully. Users should expect a calming, sleep-promoting effect within the first hour or so after dosing, and should only use it in the evening when they are ready to sleep. It should not be combined with other sedatives or sleep medications without medical guidance, and because melatonin can cause grogginess in some people, users should confirm how they respond before relying on it around activities that require alertness the next morning. Injection sites should be rotated, and anyone taking blood-pressure or sedative medication should consult a physician first.

rows.dose: 0.5 to 1 mL nightly or as needed
rows.notes: Direct-dose evening relaxation and sleep injection with no titration required. A typical protocol is 0.5 to 1 mL administered subcutaneously or intramuscularly in the evening before bed, either nightly or as needed. Do not combine with other sedatives or sleep medications without medical guidance. Rotate injection sites. Assess next-morning grogginess before relying on it.

records.name: Renisamin
records.description: Renisamin is a Khavinson cytomedin — a natural low-molecular-weight polypeptide complex extracted from the kidney tissue of young animals — developed at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology as the kidney-specific bioregulator in the Khavinson framework. It works by entering renal tubular epithelial cells and glomerular cells, binding to nuclear DNA at organ-specific gene promoter regions, and normalizing the gene expression programs that govern how those cells function, survive, and regenerate. In plain terms: the kidneys lose functional units (nephrons) with age and stress, and Renisamin signals the surviving nephron cells to behave more like young, healthy kidney cells — improving their filtration efficiency, reducing fibrotic scarring, and supporting cellular survival under metabolic stress. Renisamin has been studied primarily in two populations: aging subjects with declining kidney reserve (falling GFR without a frank CKD diagnosis) and subjects with early-to-moderate chronic kidney disease. Research outcomes include improvements in serum creatinine trends, reduction in urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratios in subjects with microalbuminuria, stimulation of renal tubular cell regeneration, and reduction in markers of tubular fibrosis. A particularly compelling line of research demonstrated Renisamin's ability to restore tubular cell function following nephrotoxic injury — including cisplatin and contrast agent-induced acute tubular damage — making it relevant not just for aging renal decline but for recovery from medically or chemotherapy-induced kidney insults. What makes Renisamin unique in this database is its position as the only Khavinson organ bioregulator targeting the kidneys with no corresponding injectable synthetic short-peptide analog commercially available — unlike the Ovagen/Svetinorm, Pancragen/Suprefort, or Vesugen/Ventfort pairs. This means Renisamin is the sole entry point for Khavinson-framework renal bioregulator support, and oral cytomedin form is the primary available delivery route. Its synergy with BPC-157 (renal angiogenic and anti-inflammatory support) and SS-31 (mitochondrial membrane protection in the energetically demanding proximal tubular cells) reflects a three-layer renal protection strategy covering gene programs (Renisamin), structural regeneration (BPC-157), and cellular energy infrastructure (SS-31) simultaneously.

Upper end (3 tablets 3x daily) for subjects with early CKD Stage 1-2 and significant proteinuria. Repeat every 3-6 months.

contraindications: eGFR < 30 (CKD Stage 4-5) without nephrologist supervision — severely reduced functional nephron mass limits bioregulator target cell availability; the altered pharmacokinetics of oral peptide absorption and renal clearance in advanced CKD require specialist oversight for dose adjustment.

Active acute kidney injury (AKI) in the anuric or oliguric phase — Renisamin is a tissue regenerative bioregulator, not an acute intervention for AKI management; initiation during active oliguric AKI has not been evaluated and could interact with the acute injury-repair process.

Renal cell carcinoma or urothelial malignancy — renal tubular cell gene program normalization activity has not been evaluated in the context of malignant renal cells; nephron bioregulator activity in malignant tissue requires oncological evaluation.

Active nephrotic syndrome with severe hypoalbuminemia (albumin < 2.0 g/dL) — the profound protein losses of active nephrotic syndrome create an unpredictable pharmacokinetic context for oral peptide absorption.
Known hypersensitivity to Renisamin (renal tissue cytomedin polypeptide complex) or formulation excipients.
Pregnancy — renal hemodynamic changes during pregnancy (50% increase in GFR, renal enlargement, altered tubular function) create an unevaluated context for exogenous renal bioregulator activity.

Renal transplantation on immunosuppression — renal tubular cell bioregulator activity in immunosuppressed recipients with donor nephron tissue requires transplant nephrology supervision; interactions with calcineurin inhibitor-induced nephrotoxicity and the immunosuppression-modified renal transcriptome are not characterized.
Active pyelonephritis or renal abscess — acute bacterial renal parenchymal infection requires antimicrobial management; bioregulator activity during active renal infection has not been characterized.

Polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) with rapidly progressive cyst expansion — the cystic epithelial proliferation mechanism of ADPKD involves specific gene dysregulation; the effect of nephron bioregulator activity on cystic versus normal tubular epithelium has not been evaluated.
sideEffects: Mild transient creatinine fluctuation — in subjects with pre-existing renal dysfunction, the initiation of nephron bioregulator activity can produce a brief transient fluctuation in serum creatinine in the first days as tubular function normalizes; typically self-limiting and below clinically significant thresholds; warrants monitoring in subjects with CKD Stage 3+ at baseline.

Mild gastrointestinal discomfort — as an oral cytomedin tablet, Renisamin is taken before meals; occasional mild gastric discomfort in the first days of a course has been reported; resolves with continued administration.

Mild increased urinary output in first cycle days — as tubular reabsorption efficiency normalizes, some subjects report mildly increased urine output in early cycle days; reflects improved tubular function rather than adverse effect; typically self-limiting.
Mild fatigue on initiation — renal metabolic reprogramming imposes a transient energy cost; mild fatigue in days 1-3 is occasionally reported; resolves rapidly.

No serious renal adverse events documented in the Khavinson research literature at standard protocol doses — Renisamin's safety profile in CKD, diabetic nephropathy, and aging renal decline populations studied over decades of Russian clinical use is clean; no serious worsening of renal function has been attributed to Renisamin in the published research.

Potential interaction with RAAS blockade — concurrent ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy combined with Renisamin's improvement in glomerular filtration efficiency could produce modest additive blood pressure and eGFR changes; clinically beneficial in most contexts but warrants monitoring of blood pressure and creatinine in the first Renisamin cycle in subjects on RAAS therapy.

Potential interaction with SGLT2 inhibitors — the complementary mechanisms of SGLT2 inhibitor intraglomerular pressure reduction and Renisamin's tubular cell gene program normalization are pharmacologically additive in a beneficial direction; combined renal protection is the expected outcome; no safety concerns documented.

records.name: Retatrutide
records.description: Retatrutide is the current frontier of incretin pharmacology — a "triple agonist" that activates three metabolic hormone receptors simultaneously: GLP-1, GIP, and the glucagon receptor. If semaglutide picks one lock and tirzepatide picks two, retatrutide picks all three at once. The GLP-1 component handles appetite suppression and slows gastric emptying, the GIP component amplifies insulin sensitivity and fat metabolism, and the glucagon receptor component — the one no other approved incretin compound touches — directly increases energy expenditure by raising your basal metabolic rate and driving thermogenesis in brown adipose tissue. The clever engineering here is that the glucagon receptor, in isolation, would raise blood sugar (glucagon is the counter-hormone to insulin). But because GLP-1 and GIP are firing simultaneously to boost insulin output, that blood sugar rise is neutralized — leaving only the thermogenic and fat-oxidizing effects of glucagon receptor activation intact. The phase 2 clinical data from the NEJM trial is the most aggressive weight loss result ever recorded for a pharmacological compound. At the 8mg and 12mg doses, subjects lost an average of 22.8% and 24.2% of total body weight over 48 weeks respectively — numbers that have never been seen with any prior drug, including tirzepatide. Visceral fat reduction, liver fat content reduction, and triglyceride improvements were all pronounced. The glucagon receptor contribution is believed to be responsible for the metabolic rate elevation that separates retatrutide's results from tirzepatide, essentially preventing the metabolic adaptation (slowing metabolism) that typically blunts weight loss over time. It is currently in Phase 3 trials for obesity, type 2 diabetes, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). The trade-off for this level of efficacy is a more demanding side effect profile, specifically around cardiovascular stress. The glucagon receptor activation elevates resting heart rate — in some subjects significantly — which is why morning dosing is preferred (to allow heart rate normalization during waking hours) and why subjects with pre-existing cardiac issues are excluded. A unique side effect not seen with other incretins is skin hyperesthesia: an unusual sensitivity to touch, particularly on the arms and torso, that emerges at higher doses. Retatrutide is not a compound for first-time incretin researchers — it is most appropriate for experienced users who have run semaglutide or tirzepatide protocols and understand their individual tolerability baseline.

records.name: Selank
records.description: Selank is a synthetic heptapeptide (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro) developed by the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences as a stabilized analog of the endogenous immunomodulatory tetrapeptide tuftsin (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg). Tuftsin is a natural fragment of IgG immunoglobulin that activates macrophage function and has CNS activity; Selank appends a Pro-Gly-Pro tripeptide tail that dramatically extends the half-life by protecting against rapid enzymatic degradation, converting a peptide with seconds-scale activity into one with meaningful pharmacokinetic duration. Selank was developed under Russia's Institute of Molecular Genetics program as an anxiolytic agent and received approval in Russia for the treatment of generalized anxiety disorder. Its primary mechanism at the neurochemical level is inhibition of enkephalinase — the enzyme that degrades enkephalins (endogenous opioid pentapeptides), thereby increasing endogenous enkephalin tone in limbic circuits without direct opioid receptor agonism. Elevated enkephalin activity in the amygdala and periaqueductal gray produces anxiolysis, emotional stabilization, and reduction in fear-conditioned responses. Selank also modulates the expression of BDNF and serotonin transporter (SERT) mRNA, providing secondary neuroprotective and mood-stabilizing effects. Crucially, Selank does not act on GABA-A receptors — the target of benzodiazepines — meaning it produces no muscle relaxation, no respiratory depression, no anticonvulsant activity, and critically, no physical dependence or withdrawal syndrome. This GABA-independence is the defining clinical advantage over traditional anxiolytics. The psychopharmacological profile of Selank is unusual in that it reduces anxiety without producing sedation, cognitive blunting, or motivational suppression — the primary complaints that lead to benzodiazepine and pregabalin discontinuation. Clinical trial data from Russian research shows that Selank improves performance on attention, processing speed, and memory tasks even while reducing anxiety scores — a combination that no conventional anxiolytic achieves. The mechanism explanation is that enkephalin potentiation selectively reduces the hyperactivation of the amygdala and anterior cingulate cortex that drives anxious rumination without suppressing the prefrontal dopaminergic and noradrenergic circuits that support executive function. This explains the synergy with Semax: Semax upregulates BDNF/TrkB/MC4R-mediated cognitive enhancement and dopaminergic activation, while Selank manages the anxiety and overstimulation that Semax can produce in sensitive subjects at higher doses — the classic "stack" using Selank as the anxiolytic brake on Semax's stimulant accelerator. The sleep protocol application of Selank (500mcg pre-bed) is mechanistically sound but operates differently from DSIP or other dedicated sleep peptides. Selank does not directly promote slow-wave sleep architecture the way DSIP does — it reduces the amygdala hyperactivation and cognitive arousal (racing thoughts, anticipatory anxiety) that prevent sleep onset in subjects with anxiety-driven insomnia. The sleep benefit is therefore most pronounced in subjects whose insomnia is anxiety-mediated rather than circadian or sleep architecture-mediated. The 4-week cycle/2-week washout is conservative given Selank's benign tolerability profile, but the enkephalinase inhibition mechanism means endogenous enkephalin tone is acutely dependent on the drug during use; the washout period allows the enkephalinase/enkephalin equilibrium to self-regulate rather than becoming permanently dependent on exogenous inhibition.

records.name: Semaglutide
records.description: Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist — meaning it mimics a hormone your body naturally produces after eating called GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1). That hormone tells your pancreas to release insulin when blood sugar rises, signals your brain that you are full, and slows down how quickly food moves out of your stomach. Semaglutide does all of those things simultaneously, but at a far greater magnitude and duration than your body does on its own. The result is a powerful and sustained reduction in appetite, improved blood sugar regulation, and significantly slower gastric emptying — all from a single weekly injection. In research, semaglutide has become the most studied and clinically validated peptide compound in the weight loss space. Subjects in the landmark STEP trials lost an average of 15–17% of total body weight over 68 weeks, which represented a category-defining result at the time. Beyond fat loss, it has demonstrated meaningful cardiovascular protection — reducing the risk of heart attack, stroke, and cardiovascular death in high-risk populations. More recent research has explored its potential in kidney disease, Alzheimer's disease, addiction pathways, and fatty liver disease (MASLD), making it one of the most broadly studied compounds in modern peptide research. What sets semaglutide apart from older GLP-1 compounds like liraglutide is its modified structure, which allows it to bind to albumin in the bloodstream and resist rapid enzymatic breakdown. This extends its active half-life to approximately one week, which is why it only needs to be dosed once weekly rather than daily. For new researchers, semaglutide is often the entry point into incretin-based protocols — it is well-characterized, has an established titration framework, and its side effect profile is predictable and manageable with a proper low-and-slow dose escalation approach.

records.name: Semax
records.description: Semax is a synthetic heptapeptide (Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro) derived from the 4–10 fragment of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) — specifically the portion responsible for ACTH's nootropic and neuroprotective effects, stripped of its adrenal-stimulating activity. Developed in Russia by the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences and approved in Russia and Ukraine as a prescription drug for stroke treatment, cognitive decline, and optic nerve disease, Semax remains one of the most clinically validated neuropeptides in this database. Its primary mechanism of action is dual: first, it directly stimulates the TrkB receptor (the high-affinity receptor for BDNF, Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor), producing downstream CREB phosphorylation, synaptic plasticity gene expression, and neuronal survival signaling. Second, Semax activates the melanocortin MC4R receptor in the brain, which enhances dopaminergic and serotonergic tone in prefrontal circuits governing executive function, attention, and working memory. Semax also increases BDNF mRNA transcription directly — producing sustained elevation in BDNF protein over the days following a dose course, which is mechanistically distinct from simply mimicking BDNF receptor activation acutely. This combination of direct TrkB agonism, MC4R activation, and transcriptional BDNF upregulation explains why Semax produces both immediate cognitive enhancement (within hours of the first dose) and cumulative neuroplasticity benefits that outlast the administration course. The clinical research base for Semax spans over three decades of Russian and Eastern European study. Published clinical data demonstrates efficacy in ischemic stroke recovery (reducing infarct-associated neural death and accelerating functional recovery), optic nerve atrophy, ADHD, and cognitive impairment. In healthy subjects, acute Semax administration increases alpha and theta EEG power, improves performance on attention, working memory, and processing speed tasks, and produces a subjective state of heightened mental clarity without the agitation characteristic of dopaminergic stimulants. The BDNF-elevating effect is particularly important from a neuroprotection standpoint: BDNF is the principal survival factor for hippocampal neurons, and declining BDNF is associated with depression, neurodegenerative disease, and stress-induced hippocampal atrophy. Semax's ability to raise BDNF significantly with a short administration course positions it as one of the most mechanistically relevant tools in this database for long-term brain health beyond acute cognitive enhancement. The contraindication with Adamax is the most practically important protocol consideration. Adamax is a highly lipophilic, potentiated derivative of Semax that achieves dramatically greater CNS penetration and BDNF upregulation through the adamantane modification — its effects overlap Semax's receptor targets almost completely but with greater magnitude and duration. Co-administering both compounds produces redundant, additive stimulation of the same TrkB/MC4R/BDNF axis without a corresponding increase in benefit, while increasing overstimulation risk (anxiety, insomnia, cardiovascular stimulation). The washout requirement before cycling exists specifically to prevent TrkB and MC4R downregulation from continuous agonism — the 2–4 week off period allows receptor density to normalize before the next course. Hair loss associated with BDNF elevation is a rarely discussed but documented phenomenon: high BDNF accelerates hair follicle cycling, which can transiently shift follicles from anagen into catagen/telogen phase, producing increased shedding that resolves after the BDNF spike normalizes.

records.name: Sermorelin
records.description: Sermorelin is the oldest and most clinically well-characterized GHRH analog in this database. It consists of the first 29 amino acids of endogenous human growth hormone-releasing hormone (hGHRH 1-29), which constitute the minimum biologically active fragment required for full GHRH receptor binding and pituitary GH stimulation. Native GHRH is 44 amino acids long, but truncation to the 29-amino acid fragment preserves complete receptor affinity while producing a shorter, more manufacturable peptide. Sermorelin was FDA-approved in the 1990s under the brand name Geref for the diagnosis of GH deficiency in children and later for the treatment of adult GH deficiency and HIV-associated wasting, giving it one of the longest and most robust human clinical safety records among all compounds in this database. As the mildest GHRH analog in this database — relative to CJC-1295 No DAC and especially tesamorelin — sermorelin produces the most physiologically conservative GH stimulation. Its half-life is approximately 10–20 minutes, meaning each injection produces a single short GHRH burst that prompts a modest GH pulse and clears quickly, with minimal risk of receptor desensitization or IGF-1 overshoot at standard doses. This makes sermorelin the preferred entry point for new researchers to the GH axis category: it has the longest safety record, the most available human clinical data, the lowest side effect ceiling, and the most predictable dose-response relationship. It is particularly appropriate for anti-aging protocols in older adults (>50) where aggressive GH stimulation may carry metabolic risks that younger subjects tolerate better. When stacked with ipamorelin, GHRP-2, or GHRP-6, sermorelin follows the same GHRH+GHRP synergy framework as CJC-1295: the GHRH-R stimulation from sermorelin and the GHS-R1a stimulation from the GHRP converge on pituitary somatotrophs to produce a significantly amplified GH pulse. The synergistic GH pulse from sermorelin + ipamorelin is smaller in absolute terms than CJC-1295 No DAC + ipamorelin, reflecting sermorelin's lower intrinsic potency — but for conservative anti-aging protocols where modest, sustainable GH elevation over many months is the goal rather than maximum GH output, this is the appropriate trade-off. It is contraindicated alongside tesamorelin, CJC-1295 (both variants), and HGH 191aa for the same GHRH receptor redundancy reasons as other GHRH analogs.

records.name: Shred (SHR)
records.description: Shred (product code SHR) is a straightforward fat-metabolism and energy injection that combines carnitine, a MIC methylation base, and B-vitamins in a balanced, non-stimulant formula. It is a vitamin and amino blend rather than a peptide, working through nutritional and metabolic pathways, and given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Each milliliter contains L-Carnitine 200mg, B12 250mcg, B6 (Pyridoxine) 25mg, Inositol 50mg, Methionine 25mg, and Choline 50mg. The carnitine supports mitochondrial fatty-acid transport, the methionine, inositol, and choline provide the lipotropic fat-mobilization base, and the B6 and B12 support amino acid metabolism, energy production, and red blood cell formation. In practice, Shred is used by people who want a clean, reliable lipotropic fat-loss injection without stimulants or beta-agonists, positioning it as a solid everyday cutting-support option. It delivers a meaningful carnitine dose alongside the classic MIC ingredients and enough B-vitamin support for an energy benefit, which makes it a popular middle-ground choice between the basic Lipo-C and the more aggressive Super Shred or Fat Blaster formulas. It is typically administered in the morning as a standing weekly injection during fat-loss phases, and because it contains no stimulants it is well tolerated by a wide range of users. Like the other lipotropic blends, it works best alongside a calorie deficit and consistent training. Mechanistically, Shred pairs a mitochondrial fatty-acid transporter (carnitine) with methyl donors (methionine, inositol, choline) and macronutrient coenzymes (B6, B12), giving the body both the raw materials and the cofactors to mobilize and burn fat while supporting energy. Users should expect gradual fat-metabolism and energy support that accumulates with consistent use rather than an acute effect. Morning administration is preferred because the carnitine and B-vitamins are mildly energizing. Injection sites should be rotated, and the standard liver, kidney, and seizure precautions apply.

A typical protocol is 0.5 to 1 mL administered subcutaneously or intramuscularly 2 to 3 times per week, in the morning. Rotate injection sites each administration. Suitable for continuous use during fat-loss phases.

records.name: Sigumir
records.description: Sigumir is a Khavinson cytomedin — peptide complex A-4 — extracted from the bone and cartilage tissue of young animals, developed at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology as the skeletal tissue bioregulator of the Khavinson framework. It works by delivering an organ-specific peptide signal directly to osteoblasts (the cells that build bone matrix) and chondrocytes (the cells that maintain cartilage), normalizing the gene expression programs that govern how these cells produce collagen, regulate bone remodeling, and maintain joint integrity. In practical terms, Sigumir tells aging bone and cartilage cells to behave more like young ones — restoring the balance between bone formation and resorption that tips toward net bone loss in osteoporosis, and maintaining the cartilage matrix synthesis that slows in osteoarthritis. Research outcomes documented in the Khavinson literature for Sigumir and predecessor bone/cartilage cytomedin preparations include improvements in bone mineral density markers in subjects with osteopenia, reduction in bone resorption markers (C-telopeptide, urinary crosslinks), increases in osteocalcin and alkaline phosphatase as markers of active bone formation, and improvement in joint mobility and pain scores in subjects with age-related joint degeneration. These findings span both the bone density and the joint function dimensions of musculoskeletal aging — making Sigumir one of the few bioregulators in this database with documented benefit across two distinct tissue types simultaneously. What distinguishes Sigumir from Cartalax — the injectable synthetic tripeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp) cartilage bioregulator also in this database — is both the route and the tissue scope. Cartalax is a precisely defined single-sequence synthetic peptide delivered subcutaneously, focused on chondrocyte gene programs; Sigumir is a broader oral cytomedin covering both osteoblast bone matrix synthesis and chondrocyte cartilage production from a single oral capsule. This makes them clinically complementary rather than interchangeable: Cartalax provides injectable precision for the cartilage layer; Sigumir provides oral coverage for the subchondral bone foundation beneath it. Together they address the full articular joint — the cartilage surface and the bone structure that supports it — which is the mechanistic rationale for their synergy designation in this database.

records.name: SLU-PP-332
records.description: SLU-PP-332 is a synthetic small molecule agonist of the Estrogen-Related Receptors (ERRα, ERRβ, ERRγ) — a family of nuclear receptors that function as constitutively active transcription factors governing the expression of genes involved in mitochondrial biogenesis, fatty acid oxidation, and oxidative phosphorylation. Despite the "estrogen-related" nomenclature, ERRs are not estrogen receptors and do not produce estrogenic effects — they are orphan nuclear receptors with no known endogenous ligand that regulate cellular energy metabolism independently of estrogen signaling. SLU-PP-332 stabilizes the co-activator recruitment surface of ERRα/β/γ, enhancing their transcriptional activity and driving expression of PGC-1α and PGC-1β target genes. This produces a wholesale transcriptional reprogramming of skeletal muscle: mitochondrial density increases, OXPHOS gene expression is upregulated, fatty acid transport proteins and beta-oxidation enzymes are induced, and slow-twitch oxidative fiber gene programs are activated — the molecular signature of endurance-trained skeletal muscle, achieved without the mechanical stimulus of training. The 2023 Washington University research that characterized SLU-PP-332 showed treated mice ran significantly farther and faster than controls with histological evidence of increased slow-twitch fiber content and mitochondrial density, alongside 10% body weight reductions in obese mice and improved insulin sensitivity — all without changes in food intake. The ERR agonist mechanism is architecturally distinct from the AMPK-based exercise mimetics (AICAR, MOTS-c) also in this database. AICAR and MOTS-c activate AMPK kinase signaling — a rapid, cytoplasmic cascade that produces metabolic shifts within hours and clears with the compound. SLU-PP-332 operates upstream at the nuclear transcription factor level: it rewrites the gene expression program of muscle cells over days to weeks of persistent new protein synthesis. This means onset of effect is slower but the metabolic reprogramming is more durable — lasting beyond compound clearance as the newly synthesized mitochondrial proteins and slow-twitch structural proteins persist. The synergy with MOTS-c and 5-Amino-1MQ is mechanistically layered: SLU-PP-332 builds the mitochondrial infrastructure (biogenesis), MOTS-c activates the acute metabolic switching signals (AMPK/GLUT4/fat oxidation), and 5-Amino-1MQ ensures the NAD+ substrate pool is not depleted by NNMT activity — three independent entry points into the same metabolic upgrade converging on fat oxidation and mitochondrial performance. SLU-PP-332 is the most experimentally early-stage compound in this entire database from a human data standpoint. As of mid-2026, there are no published Phase 1 human clinical trials — all mechanistic and efficacy data extrapolates from cell culture and rodent studies. Human pharmacokinetics, bioavailability by route, metabolic clearance, drug-drug interactions, and the full safety profile are genuinely unknown at the clinical level. The availability of both oral tablet and injectable subcutaneous formulations reflects SLU-PP-332's small molecule (non-peptide) architecture — unlike peptides that require injection due to GI degradation, small molecules like SLU-PP-332 may retain meaningful oral bioavailability, and the multiple oral titration protocols in this database use progressively divided daily doses to maintain sustained ERR activation throughout the day rather than a single peak-and-trough cycle. The cardiac ERR activity warrants specific note: ERRα is highly expressed in cardiac muscle where it drives the OXPHOS gene program that keeps the heart in its preferred oxidative metabolic state — this is potentially beneficial in heart failure, but the consequences of supraphysiological ERR agonism in diseased cardiac tissue remain uncharacterized.

rows.notes: Administered in the morning or pre-workout.

protocols.label: Alternative Titration 1 - 60mg Week Max Oral Tabs

contraindications: Active malignancy — ERRα is overexpressed in multiple cancers including breast, ovarian, and prostate cancer where it promotes tumor survival, metastasis, and OXPHOS upregulation that supports tumor bioenergetics; SLU-PP-332's ERR agonism could activate these same pro-tumor transcriptional programs.

Hormone-sensitive cancers (breast, ovarian, prostate, endometrial) — while ERRs are mechanistically distinct from estrogen receptors, they share pathway convergence in hormone-sensitive tissues and have documented roles in driving progression of these cancers.
Pregnancy — ERR nuclear receptors are involved in trophoblast development and placental energy metabolism; exogenous ERR agonism during pregnancy is not established as safe.
Breastfeeding — no safety data established.
Known hypersensitivity to SLU-PP-332 or related quinazolinone compounds.

Severe cardiac arrhythmia or decompensated heart failure — ERRα is highly expressed in cardiac tissue and drives the cardiac OXPHOS gene program; in decompensated heart failure where cardiac energy metabolism is already dysregulated, supraphysiological ERR agonism may produce uncharacterized and potentially adverse effects.
Pediatric use — ERR receptors are involved in developmental biology; safety in children is not established.
Concurrent use with other PGC-1α or ERR-modulating agents — the magnitude of overlapping mitochondrial biogenesis stimulation from multiple simultaneous pathway activators is not characterized.
sideEffects: Mild lethargy post-dose during initiation — the metabolic reprogramming demands cellular resources during the gene expression transition phase; most pronounced in weeks 1–2 as new mitochondrial proteins are being synthesized; resolves as the oxidative capacity becomes established.
Injection site irritation — redness, soreness, minor swelling at subcutaneous administration site; standard response.

Insomnia or sleep disruption — ERR agonism and mitochondrial biogenesis drive upregulated metabolic rate; dosing in the afternoon or evening may produce difficulty falling asleep; morning and pre-workout dosing protocols exist specifically to prevent this.

GI discomfort with oral tablet formulations — nausea, abdominal bloating, or loose stools at higher oral doses; the split oral dosing schedules (morning, 11am, 2pm) distribute the load to reduce peak GI exposure.

Potential cardiovascular effects — ERRα's cardiac expression means SLU-PP-332 has cardiac metabolic activity; in healthy subjects this is likely beneficial but cardiac effects in diseased tissue are not characterized.

Theoretical ERR-mediated cancer cell activation — the most significant theoretical adverse concern; the same transcriptional programs SLU-PP-332 activates for metabolic benefit in healthy tissue overlap with pro-tumor ERRα programs in oncological contexts.

Unknown long-term adverse effects — no published Phase 1 human clinical trial data exists as of mid-2026; the complete human adverse event profile is genuinely uncharacterized beyond animal studies and early research observation.

No estrogenic side effects — despite the "estrogen-related" nomenclature, SLU-PP-332 does not activate ERα or ERβ estrogen receptors and produces no estrogenic effects (gynecomastia, feminization, HPTA suppression).

records.name: SNAP-8
records.description: SNAP-8 (acetyl octapeptide-3) is a synthetic octapeptide (Ac-Glu-Glu-Met-Gln-Arg-Arg-Ala-Asp-NH₂) designed as a topical competitive inhibitor of the SNARE (Soluble NSF Attachment Protein REceptor) complex — the molecular machinery that mediates synaptic vesicle fusion and neurotransmitter release at the neuromuscular junction. The mechanism directly parallels the action of Botulinum toxin (Botox/onabotulinumtoxinA), but through a reversible and topically deliverable competitive inhibition rather than irreversible enzymatic cleavage. Botulinum toxin works by cleaving SNAP-25 (Synaptosomal-Associated Protein 25) — a key SNARE complex component on the presynaptic nerve terminal — preventing acetylcholine vesicle fusion and producing the flaccid muscle paralysis that reduces dynamic facial wrinkles. SNAP-8 mimics the N-terminal end of SNAP-25 (residues 12–19 of the SNAP-25 sequence), competing with native SNAP-25 for the binding sites on synaptobrevin (VAMP) and syntaxin within the SNARE complex — partially inhibiting SNARE complex formation and reducing but not eliminating acetylcholine release at the motor endplate. The result is graded, partial, reversible reduction in facial muscle contraction intensity — sufficient to reduce the depth of dynamic expression wrinkles (crow's feet, forehead lines, glabellar furrows) while preserving natural facial expressivity, without the risk of ptosis, facial asymmetry, or diffusion-related adverse effects associated with injected botulinum toxin. The topical delivery pharmacology of SNAP-8 is the critical determinant of its efficacy — the octapeptide must penetrate the 10–20 μm stratum corneum barrier to reach the dermal-epidermal junction where motor nerve terminals synapse on facial muscle fibers. The acetyl N-terminal modification (Ac-) improves lipophilicity slightly versus the unmodified peptide, but SNAP-8 relies primarily on passive diffusion through skin penetration enhancers in the carrier vehicle (propylene glycol, glycerin, sodium PCA, sodium hyaluronate) and the relatively small molecular weight of the octapeptide (approximately 1076 Da) to achieve transdermal delivery. The 3–10% concentration range reflects the dose-response relationship: at 3% SNAP-8 provides measurable wrinkle reduction over 8–12 weeks of daily use; at 10% the competition with native SNAP-25 is sufficient to produce comparable wrinkle depth reduction to low-dose Botox injections in some clinical evaluations. The synergy with Matrixyl is the most mechanistically complete topical anti-aging combination: SNAP-8 addresses the neuromuscular component of dynamic wrinkle formation (reducing the muscle contraction that creates the wrinkle), while Matrixyl addresses the structural collagen loss that makes wrinkles permanent even at rest — together preventing new dynamic wrinkle deepening (SNAP-8) while simultaneously repairing the existing structural deficit that has made current wrinkles static (Matrixyl). The safety profile of SNAP-8 versus injectable Botulinum toxin represents one of the most favorable risk comparisons in aesthetic medicine: Botox carries risks of eyelid ptosis (upper lid drooping from toxin diffusion to the levator palpebrae), facial asymmetry from uneven diffusion, dysphagia and dysphonia with forehead or neck injections, spread to distant muscles, and very rarely systemic botulism-like effects; SNAP-8's topical competitive inhibition mechanism is intrinsically self-limiting because it cannot diffuse beyond the application area, cannot produce irreversible SNAP-25 cleavage, and cannot achieve the neuromuscular blockade depth that produces ptosis or paralysis. The reversibility is inherent: as SNAP-8 concentration at the neuromuscular junction declines with skin cell turnover and normal metabolic clearance (half-life at the target is hours to days, not weeks like Botox), the SNARE competitive inhibition reverses and muscle function fully recovers — continuous daily application is required to maintain the effect.

rows.notes: Use 3% to 10% concentration in a topical vehicle (lotion or serum).

washout: Cycle Length: Indefinite.
Washout: None.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to SNAP-8 (acetyl octapeptide-3), methionine-containing peptides, or carrier vehicle excipients.

Active neuromuscular disease affecting facial muscles (myasthenia gravis, Lambert-Eaton syndrome, ALS) — SNAP-8's inhibition of neuromuscular acetylcholine release in subjects with pre-existing neuromuscular junction dysfunction could compound existing muscle weakness.

Concurrent botulinum toxin injections in the same treatment area — SNAP-8's SNARE competitive inhibition is additive with Botulinum toxin's SNAP-25 cleavage; while the combination theoretically produces greater muscle relaxation, the combined neuromuscular blockade at the same anatomical sites has not been characterized for safety and could produce unexpected depth of paralysis.

Active dermatitis, eczema, or psoriasis in the application area — compromised barrier function increases peptide penetration and could produce enhanced neuromuscular effects beyond the intended level.
Open wounds or compromised skin in the application area.

Application near or in the eyes without ophthalmic safety evaluation — SNAP-25 is expressed in multiple neuronal populations beyond facial motor neurons; periocular application in quantities reaching the conjunctiva or anterior chamber without ophthalmic testing is inadvisable.
sideEffects: Mild skin irritation and erythema — less common than with Matrixyl; occasional in sensitive subjects with certain carrier vehicle formulations; typically related to penetration enhancer components (propylene glycol) rather than the peptide itself.
Mild tingling on application — transient; as the octapeptide penetrates the stratum corneum; not indicative of irritation.

Slight facial heaviness or reduced expressivity — in subjects applying high concentrations (8–10%) to multiple facial zones simultaneously, the partial neuromuscular inhibition can produce a subjective sensation of mild facial muscle heaviness; entirely reversible; resolves within hours if application is discontinued.
Contact dermatitis (rare) — delayed hypersensitivity to peptide components; documented rarely; requires patch testing and permanent avoidance of the specific formulation.

No systemic adverse effects — topical application with intact skin barrier limits systemic absorption to levels far below any pharmacologically active concentration; SNAP-8 is among the safest compounds in the database from a systemic safety standpoint.

Tolerance with long-term continuous use (theoretical) — the SNAP-25 competitive inhibition mechanism is reversible and receptor-mediated; theoretical tachyphylaxis from downregulation of SNAP-25 or neuromuscular junction adaptation with prolonged continuous high-concentration application has not been documented in clinical use but represents a mechanistic consideration for very long-term protocols.

records.name: SS-31 (Elamipretide)
records.description: SS-31 (elamipretide, Szeto-Schiller peptide 31) is a tetrapeptide (D-Arg-2'6'-dimethylTyr-Lys-Phe-NH₂) that selectively accumulates in the inner mitochondrial membrane (IMM) through electrostatic interaction driven by the large negative mitochondrial membrane potential (approximately -180 mV). This selectivity is the defining pharmacological property of SS-31: while most molecules cannot penetrate the double-membrane architecture of mitochondria, SS-31's cationic charge and alternating aromatic residue design drives it specifically to the IMM at concentrations 5,000-fold higher than cytoplasmic levels. The molecular target at the IMM is cardiolipin — a unique tetra-acyl phospholipid found almost exclusively in the inner mitochondrial membrane that is essential for structuring the electron transport chain complexes (particularly Complex I and Complex IV) and stabilizing the curvature of the IMM cristae. Cardiolipin becomes oxidized and dysfunctional in aging, ischemia-reperfusion injury, heart failure, and mitochondrial disease — and this oxidation is a primary driver of mitochondrial structural collapse, proton leak, impaired ATP synthesis, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) overproduction. SS-31 binds to cardiolipin, protects it from oxidation, and restores the structural architecture that allows efficient electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation. The downstream effects of cardiolipin stabilization by SS-31 are measurable across multiple organ systems. In cardiac muscle, SS-31 reduces infarct size in ischemia-reperfusion models by up to 40%, preserves mitochondrial morphology after myocardial ischemia, and reduces the ROS burst that drives reperfusion injury. In skeletal muscle, SS-31 restores exercise capacity in aged animals to levels comparable to young controls — reflecting the reversal of age-related mitochondrial dysfunction that limits muscular endurance. In the kidney, elamipretide (SS-31) has advanced to Phase 2/3 clinical trials for mitochondria-associated cardiomyopathy (Barth syndrome) and for primary mitochondrial myopathy — making it the most clinically advanced compound in Category IV. The therapeutic logic is consistent: wherever cells are energy-intensive (heart, muscle, kidney, brain, retina), cardiolipin deterioration with age or disease represents a rate-limiting constraint on function, and SS-31 addresses that constraint at its structural source rather than compensating for it downstream. SS-31's rationale as the "infrastructure repair" compound in a mitochondrial stack is that it enables the other compounds in the stack to work more efficiently. NAD+ supplementation increases the substrate for oxidative phosphorylation, but if the electron transport chain complexes are destabilized by oxidized cardiolipin, the additional NAD+/NADH is poorly utilized — electrons leak out as superoxide rather than being channeled efficiently to ATP production. MOTS-c drives AMPK activation and mitochondrial biogenesis, but newly synthesized mitochondria with structurally compromised IMMs replicate the dysfunction rather than resolving it. By repairing cardiolipin integrity first, SS-31 ensures the mitochondrial architecture is physically capable of capitalizing on the metabolic and biogenesis signals that MOTS-c and NAD+ provide — which is the mechanistic basis for the SS-31 → MOTS-c → NAD+ stack synergy.
