No significant systemic adverse effects documented in Phase 2/3 clinical trial data — the clinical trial program for elamipretide (SS-31) in Barth syndrome and primary mitochondrial myopathy has demonstrated a favorable tolerability profile with no dose-limiting toxicities or serious adverse events attributed to the compound in published interim data.

Potential for pathological energy provision to tumor cells (theoretical) — the mechanistic concern for cancer contraindication; not documented as a clinical adverse event.

records.name: Super Human Blend (SHB)
records.description: The Super Human Blend (product code SHB) is a comprehensive amino acid injection built for performance, recovery, and circulation, combining nine amino acids into a single administration. It is an amino acid blend rather than a peptide, working through nutritional and metabolic support, and given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Each milliliter contains L-Arginine 110mg, L-Ornithine 110mg, L-Citrulline 120mg, L-Lysine 70mg, L-Glutamine 40mg, L-Proline 60mg, L-Taurine 60mg, L-Carnitine 220mg, and NAC 75mg. Arginine, ornithine, and citrulline form a nitric oxide and growth hormone support axis that improves blood flow and recovery, lysine and proline support collagen and connective tissue, glutamine supports recovery and gut health, taurine supports cellular hydration and cardiovascular function, carnitine supports fat metabolism and energy, and NAC provides antioxidant and glutathione precursor support. In practice, the Super Human Blend is used by athletes and hard-training individuals who want broad amino acid support for training performance, recovery, blood flow, and connective tissue health in one injection rather than taking many separate products. The arginine, ornithine, and citrulline combination is particularly valued for supporting nitric oxide production, which enhances pumps and nutrient delivery during training, and for supporting the natural growth hormone response. It is typically administered in the morning or before training to align the circulation and performance benefits with activity. This blend is popular during both building and recovery phases because its profile supports tissue repair, endurance, and vascular health simultaneously. Mechanistically, SHB layers several complementary amino acid actions: nitric oxide and growth hormone support (arginine, ornithine, citrulline), connective tissue and collagen support (lysine, proline), recovery and immune support (glutamine), cardiovascular and cellular hydration support (taurine), fat metabolism (carnitine), and antioxidant defense (NAC). The result is a wide-spectrum recovery and performance blend. Users should expect cumulative improvements in recovery, training capacity, and blood flow with consistent use rather than a single acute effect, though the vasodilatory aminos can produce a noticeable pump when dosed before training. Injection sites should be rotated, and because arginine, citrulline, and taurine can lower blood pressure and NAC can thin mucus and mildly affect clotting, anyone on antihypertensive or anticoagulant medication should consult a physician first.

rows.notes: Direct-dose amino acid performance and recovery injection with no titration required. A typical protocol is 0.5 to 1 mL administered subcutaneously or intramuscularly 3 to 5 times per week, in the morning or before training. Rotate injection sites each administration. Suitable for continuous use during building or recovery phases.

contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to any component amino acid or formulation excipient.

Use of anticoagulant medication without physician oversight, due to the NAC content.

records.name: Super Shred (LC553)
records.description: Super Shred (product code LC553) is an advanced thermogenic fat-loss injection that pairs a strong lipotropic and cellular-energy base with albuterol, a beta-agonist bronchodilator used off-label for its fat-mobilizing and metabolic-rate effects. It is a vitamin, amino, and pharmaceutical blend rather than a peptide, delivered as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Each milliliter contains L-Carnitine 400mg, a MIC blend at 100mg, ATP 50mg, Albuterol 2mg, and B12 (Methylcobalamin) 1mg. The very high carnitine dose plus MIC base provides potent lipotropic fat transport, ATP supplies cellular energy substrate, B12 supports energy metabolism, and the albuterol adds a thermogenic, metabolism-raising component that distinguishes this as one of the more aggressive blends in the category. In practice, LC553 is chosen by experienced users seeking maximum fat-loss support during a hard cutting phase, particularly those who want a thermogenic edge beyond what standard lipotropic blends provide. The albuterol content means it has a genuine pharmacological stimulant and thermogenic action, so it is not a beginner blend and demands respect for its cardiovascular effects. It is typically dosed in the morning only and used in shorter, targeted phases rather than indefinitely, given the albuterol component. Users often assess tolerance carefully and avoid combining it with other stimulants or beta-agonists. Mechanistically, LC553 combines lipotropic fat transport (carnitine and MIC), cellular energy support (ATP and B12), and beta-agonist thermogenesis (albuterol), which can raise metabolic rate and support fat mobilization while also stimulating the cardiovascular system. Users should expect a noticeable thermogenic and mildly stimulant effect in addition to the lipotropic support. Because of the albuterol, this blend must be dosed in the morning only, never late in the day, and should be avoided by anyone with cardiovascular conditions, high blood pressure, arrhythmia, thyroid disease, or stimulant sensitivity. Injection sites should be rotated, other stimulants should be minimized on dosing days, and use should be limited to defined phases under informed, cautious conditions.

rows.notes: Direct-dose thermogenic lipotropic injection with no titration required. A typical protocol is 0.5 to 1 mL administered subcutaneously or intramuscularly up to 3 times per week, in the morning only, due to the albuterol content. Assess tolerance with a lower volume first. Best used in defined phases rather than indefinitely. Rotate injection sites. Do not combine with other stimulants or beta-agonists.

records.name: Suprefort
records.description: Suprefort is a Khavinson cytomedin — peptide complex A-1 — extracted from the pancreatic tissue of young animals, developed as the oral pancreatic bioregulator of the Khavinson framework and the commercial predecessor to Pancragen (the injectable synthetic tetrapeptide Lys-Glu-Asp-Pro). It delivers a mixture of pancreatic tissue-derived low-molecular-weight peptides that interact with both the endocrine pancreas (the insulin-producing beta cells of the islets of Langerhans) and the exocrine pancreas (the acinar cells producing digestive enzymes), normalizing the gene expression programs governing beta cell glucose sensing, insulin synthesis and secretion, beta cell survival, and the production of digestive enzymes including lipase, amylase, and protease. In practical terms, Suprefort signals aging or damaged pancreatic cells to restore the functional program of young, healthy pancreatic tissue. Suprefort carries the longest published clinical evidence base of all pancreatic bioregulators in this database, predating Pancragen by several years of clinical use. Documented outcomes include normalization of fasting and post-prandial blood glucose in subjects with T2DM and prediabetes, improvement in pancreatic exocrine enzyme outputs measured by fecal elastase normalization, reduction in abdominal symptoms in subjects with chronic pancreatitis, and improvement in metabolic syndrome components including lipid profiles and insulin sensitivity. Because it was the original source material from which the Pancragen synthetic sequence was later isolated, Suprefort's evidence base directly supports the biological activity of its bioactive peptide content — providing decades of real-world human clinical context that purely synthetic compounds like Pancragen lack in equivalent depth. Suprefort's defining clinical role relative to Pancragen is the oral route and the broader tissue extract scope. Pancragen delivers the defined single-sequence synthetic tetrapeptide by injection with precision; Suprefort delivers the full pancreatic cytomedin matrix orally, covering both endocrine and exocrine pancreatic compartments simultaneously from a single pre-meal capsule. For subjects preferring oral-only protocols, Suprefort is the complete pancreatic bioregulator. For subjects with significant metabolic disease on injectable protocols, Suprefort can be stacked with Pancragen — the oral cytomedin breadth (Suprefort) plus the injectable synthetic peptide precision (Pancragen) — for the most complete pancreatic bioregulator coverage available. The synergy with GLP-1 agonists (semaglutide, tirzepatide) is particularly relevant: GLP-1 agonists amplify the incretin signal stimulating beta cells to secrete insulin; Suprefort normalizes the quality and health of those beta cells themselves.

rows.notes: Standard intensive course. For chronic pancreatitis: 1-2 capsules 1-2x daily before meals for 1 month. For T2DM: 2 capsules 1-2x daily before meals for 1 month, with blood glucose monitoring. Repeat every 4-6 months.

records.name: Survodutide
records.description: Survodutide (BI 456906) is a dual GLP-1 and glucagon receptor agonist developed by Boehringer Ingelheim, and it takes a structurally distinct approach from other dual agonists like mazdutide. While mazdutide is derived from a GLP-1 backbone, survodutide is built on a glucagon peptide backbone with modifications added to confer GLP-1 receptor activity — meaning it leads with glucagon agonism and adds GLP-1 on top, rather than the reverse. The practical effect of this design is a strongly glucagon-weighted dual mechanism: aggressive hepatic fat oxidation, meaningful increases in resting energy expenditure and thermogenesis, combined with the appetite suppression and gastric slowing of GLP-1 signaling. The two pathways counterbalance each other metabolically — the GLP-1 component prevents the hyperglycemia that pure glucagon activation would cause, while glucagon drives the calorie-burning effects that GLP-1 alone cannot produce. Phase 2 clinical data has positioned survodutide as one of the most potent dual agonists currently in development. At the highest studied dose, subjects achieved up to 18.7% mean body weight reduction and HbA1c reductions of up to 1.71% — results that directly outperformed semaglutide in head-to-head comparisons within the same trial framework. Its MASH profile is particularly notable: a Phase 2b MASH trial demonstrated statistically significant improvement in liver histology without worsening of fibrosis, and its anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic effects in the liver are believed to extend beyond simple fat reduction to direct tissue-level remodeling. Emerging cardiovascular data also suggests potential benefits in epicardial adiposity, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), and cardiorenal syndrome, making it one of the most broadly targeted cardiometabolic compounds currently in Phase 3 development. What distinguishes survodutide within this compound class is the severity of its appetite suppression. Researchers consistently report more aggressive hunger blunting compared to equivalent doses of pure GLP-1 agonists — a consequence of the glucagon component acting on central appetite circuits in addition to the GLP-1 pathways. The trade-off is a higher rate of GI adverse events, particularly nausea (reported in 40–66% of subjects at therapeutic doses) and vomiting (15–41%), along with a modest but consistent elevation in resting heart rate. Morning dosing is recommended to allow glucagon-driven cardiovascular stimulation to dissipate before sleep. Researchers transitioning from semaglutide or tirzepatide should expect a meaningfully different and more pronounced tolerability challenge during the escalation phase.

records.name: Svetinorm
records.description: Svetinorm is a Khavinson cytomedin — peptide complex A-7 — extracted from liver tissue of young animals, developed as the oral hepatic bioregulator of the Khavinson framework and the commercial predecessor to Ovagen (the injectable synthetic tripeptide Ile-Glu-Pro). It works by delivering a mixture of liver tissue-derived low-molecular-weight peptides that interact with hepatocytes at the transcriptional level, normalizing the gene expression programs governing hepatocyte survival, CYP450 detoxification enzyme expression, mitochondrial function, anti-fibrotic signaling (suppressing TGF-β-driven hepatic stellate cell activation that drives scarring), and lipid and glucose metabolism. In plain terms, Svetinorm signals aging or metabolically stressed liver cells to restore the functional gene activity pattern of young, healthy hepatocytes — improving detoxification capacity, metabolic efficiency, and regenerative ability. Svetinorm carries the longer clinical evidence base of the two hepatic bioregulators in this database, having been developed and used clinically before Ovagen was isolated as its synthetic bioactive core. Published research outcomes include improvements in ALT and AST in subjects with elevated transaminases, improvement in hepatic steatosis in NAFLD populations, normalization of GGT as a marker of hepatic oxidative stress, improvement in serum albumin reflecting restored synthetic function, and normalization of lipid profiles — consistent with restoration of normal hepatocyte gene programs across metabolic, synthetic, and detoxification dimensions simultaneously. Professor Khavinson specifically documented recommending Svetinorm in combination with Ventfort (vascular cytomedin) as a paired metabolic-cardiovascular protocol, reflecting the clinical reality that liver metabolic output and vascular endothelial health are biologically coupled. What distinguishes Svetinorm from Ovagen — the injectable tripeptide hepatic bioregulator also in this database — is the same oral/injectable cytomedin-vs-synthetic-peptide distinction that characterizes all the Khavinson pairs. Ovagen delivers the defined single-sequence injectable precision for subjects on injection protocols; Svetinorm delivers the full liver tissue extract oral convenience covering both the Ovagen sequence and the additional hepatic cytomedin peptide components not captured in the minimized synthetic sequence. Svetinorm is uniquely notable as the starting material from which Ovagen was reverse-engineered — meaning the published evidence for Ovagen's bioactivity is directly traceable back to the original Svetinorm cytomedin activity that produced it, and subjects using Svetinorm are benefiting from the same tissue-derived peptide repertoire that informed four decades of Khavinson liver bioregulator research.

records.name: Taxorest
records.description: Taxorest is a Khavinson cytomedin — peptide complex A-19 — extracted from the bronchial mucosal tissue of young animals, developed as the oral bronchopulmonary bioregulator of the Khavinson framework and the commercial cytomedin counterpart to Bronchogen (the injectable synthetic tetrapeptide Ala-Glu-Asp-Leu). It delivers a mixture of bronchial tissue-derived low-molecular-weight peptides that interact with bronchial epithelial cells at the transcriptional level, normalizing the gene expression programs governing ciliary function, mucus composition and production, barrier integrity, anti-inflammatory secretory profiles, and the regenerative capacity of bronchial epithelial progenitor cells. In practical terms, Taxorest signals aging airway epithelial cells to restore the protective, self-cleaning respiratory surface that years of accumulated environmental, inflammatory, or infectious damage have progressively eroded. Research and clinical outcomes documented for Taxorest and predecessor bronchial cytomedin preparations include improvement in spirometric parameters (FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC ratio) in subjects with COPD and chronic bronchitis, improvement in mucociliary clearance measured by saccharin transit time, normalization of bronchial epithelial cytology, reduction in exacerbation frequency in obstructive airways disease, and reduction in respiratory infection frequency in aging subjects with declining respiratory reserve. The sublingual lingual form of Taxorest is specifically designed to exploit direct mucosal absorption under the tongue, bypassing hepatic first-pass metabolism and potentially achieving more rapid systemic availability of the bronchial bioregulator peptides than standard enteric capsule absorption. The distinction between Taxorest and Bronchogen in this database follows the same oral/injectable cytomedin-vs-synthetic-peptide pattern seen across all Khavinson pairs, but with one additional dimension worth noting. Taxorest is specifically associated with the conducting airway epithelium — the bronchi and bronchioles — while Chonluten (the alveolar peptide bioregulator, also in this database) targets the gas-exchange alveolar epithelium. This anatomical complementarity is why Taxorest and Chonluten appear as synergistic in this database: Taxorest restores the upper and middle conducting airway epithelium that channels air; Chonluten restores the terminal alveolar epithelium where gas exchange actually occurs. For subjects with significant respiratory disease affecting both compartments — COPD, post-COVID pulmonary damage, smoking history — combining Taxorest and Chonluten provides complete bronchopulmonary coverage from airway to alveolus.

rows.notes: Standard intensive course (oral capsule form). Sublingual lingual form: 5-6 drops (0.25-0.35 ml) under tongue 3-4x daily, 10-15 minutes before meals for 1 month. Repeat every 3-6 months. For chronic disease: 2-3 courses per year.

records.name: TB-500 (Thymosin Beta-4)
records.description: TB-500 is the synthetic analog of Thymosin Beta-4 (Tβ4) — a 43 amino acid protein that is among the most abundant peptides in human cells and is present in virtually every mammalian tissue. TB-500 represents the active sequence region of Tβ4 responsible for its primary biological functions. Thymosin Beta-4 was originally identified in thymic tissue as part of the immune regulation machinery, but its most critical role — and the one relevant to this context — is as the principal regulator of G-actin sequestration. Actin is the structural protein that drives cellular motility: every cell that migrates, every wound edge that contracts, and every tissue remodeling event in the body requires the dynamic assembly and disassembly of actin filaments. TB-500 binds G-actin (the monomeric form) with extremely high affinity, maintaining a pool of available actin monomers that cells can rapidly mobilize for migration. This makes TB-500 fundamentally systemic in its mechanism — rather than acting on a specific receptor in a specific tissue, it potentiates the universal cellular repair machinery used by fibroblasts, endothelial cells, keratinocytes, and immune cells throughout the entire body simultaneously. The downstream consequences of TB-500's actin-sequestering and cell migration-promoting activity are broad: faster wound closure across all tissue types, reduced systemic inflammation via TGF-beta pathway modulation, accelerated tendon and muscle fiber repair, improved range of motion and flexibility in injured tissue, enhanced hair follicle activation, and — through upregulation of angiogenic factors — promotion of new blood vessel formation in ischemic or injured tissue. In animal models, Tβ4 has been shown to reduce cardiac fibrosis following myocardial infarction and promote cardiomyocyte survival, making cardiac recovery a legitimate research application. Unlike BPC-157, which concentrates heavily on specific tissue types (especially GI and tendons), TB-500 operates across a broader tissue distribution with a more diffuse systemic healing signal, which is why its standard protocols use loading-phase doses (4–5mg/week) followed by maintenance doses rather than injury-specific localization. TB-500 and BPC-157 are the most commonly co-administered compounds in repair-focused research protocols, and their synergy is mechanistically logical: BPC-157 drives angiogenesis and fibroblast activity via VEGF/NO pathways while TB-500 drives cellular migration and actin-mediated tissue remodeling via a completely separate pathway. These two mechanisms address complementary phases of tissue repair — vascularization and structural rebuilding — producing additive effects with no pathway competition or receptor overlap. The 8–12 week cycle length reflects the time required for the systemic healing state to fully establish and the maintenance phase to consolidate structural gains before the washout period.

rows.notes: Loading Phase (Total of 4mg - 5mg per week).
Maintenance Phase to hold systemic healing state.
Keeps blood plasma levels perfectly stable, mitigating the 'head rush' some users feel from macro-dosing twice a week.

washout: Cycle Length: 8 to 12 weeks.
Washout: 4 weeks off.
contraindications: Active cancer or high cancer risk — TB-500 promotes cell migration and angiogenesis via actin-mediated cellular motility and TGF-beta modulation; these mechanisms that accelerate healing in normal tissue also accelerate tumor cell migration, invasion, and neovascularization in malignant tissue.
History of malignancy — the pro-migratory and pro-angiogenic mechanisms present theoretical risk of stimulating dormant or residual tumor cells; assess with care.

Active cancer treatment (chemotherapy or radiation) — TB-500's pro-migratory cell effects may theoretically interfere with cytotoxic therapy mechanisms by protecting cancer cells from treatment-induced damage.
Pregnancy — no safety data; avoid.
Breastfeeding — no safety data; avoid.
Known hypersensitivity to Thymosin Beta-4, TB-500, or peptide excipients.
Anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy — potential additive effect via actin-mediated platelet function modulation; theoretical, but warrants monitoring.
Proliferative vascular disorders — subjects with pathological neovascularization or arteriovenous malformations.
Active autoimmune disorders — TB-500's immune modulatory properties (particularly TGF-beta modulation) carry theoretical risk of unpredictable immune activation in autoimmune-susceptible subjects.
Pediatric use — no safety or efficacy data established.
sideEffects: Lethargy and fatigue immediately following injection — the most commonly reported adverse effect; estimated 15–25% of users anecdotally; typically within 1–2 hours post-injection; resolves within the same day; related to the acute inflammatory modulation signal.

Head rush or vasodilation sensation — warmth or blood rushing to the head within minutes of injection; reported in a minority of users; more common with macro-dose twice-weekly protocols than with daily micro-dosing; caused by angiogenic/vasodilatory mechanism; the daily micro-dosing protocol was specifically developed to mitigate this effect.
Temporary dizziness — associated with the vasodilation response; transient.
Injection site irritation — redness, minor swelling at subcutaneous injection site; estimated 20–30% of users anecdotally; normal tissue response.
Headache — rare; less than 10% anecdotally; transient; likely vasodilation-mediated.
Nausea — rare; less than 5% anecdotally; usually dose-related; less common than with BPC-157.

Theoretical cancer cell migration risk — the most significant theoretical adverse effect; actin-mediated cell motility enhancement does not distinguish between healthy and malignant cells; this is the mechanistic basis for the cancer contraindication.
Theoretical angiogenesis in pathological contexts — new vessel formation that supports wound healing in normal tissue could support tumor vascularization in oncological contexts.

No significant hormonal side effects — unlike GH axis compounds, TB-500 does not affect the endocrine system, does not elevate cortisol or prolactin, and does not suppress natural hormonal production.
No receptor desensitization — no documented downregulation of target pathways with standard cycle lengths; efficacy does not attenuate within a single cycle.

records.name: Teriparatide (PTH 1-34)
records.description: Teriparatide is recombinant human parathyroid hormone (1-34) — the biologically active N-terminal fragment of PTH, synthesized to be sequence-identical to the first 34 amino acids of the 84-amino-acid endogenous hormone. Endogenous PTH is produced by the parathyroid glands in response to hypocalcemia and acts on the PTH1 receptor (PTH1R) expressed on osteoblasts, renal tubular cells, and other tissues to regulate calcium and phosphate homeostasis. The critical pharmacological distinction that makes teriparatide an anabolic bone agent — rather than a catabolic one — is the dosing pattern. Continuous PTH exposure (as occurs in primary hyperparathyroidism) drives net bone resorption: osteoclast activity dominates, trabecular bone is consumed, and cortical bone becomes porous. Intermittent, low-dose PTH — the precise administration pattern of the 20 mcg once-daily subcutaneous injection — produces the opposite effect: it preferentially stimulates osteoblast differentiation, proliferation, and survival through activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway and downregulation of sclerostin, resulting in net bone formation with increases in bone mineral density of 9–13% at the lumbar spine and 2.8–3.8% at the hip over 18–24 months of treatment. This pulsatile PTH-receptor stimulation paradigm is unique in pharmacology and explains why rigid adherence to the standard 20 mcg daily dose (never more frequently, never as a continuous infusion) is mandatory. Teriparatide is the most clinically validated compound in this database for its approved indication. It holds FDA approval (Forteo, Bonsity) for treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women, men with primary or hypogonadal osteoporosis, and glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis — all conditions associated with high fracture risk. Its off-label research use for accelerating bone fracture healing and stress fracture recovery is biologically logical: the same osteoblast-stimulating signaling that rebuilds osteoporotic trabecular architecture also accelerates callus formation and cortical bridge remodeling at fracture sites. Case series and small clinical studies have shown accelerated radiographic healing of stress fractures (particularly navicular and femoral neck stress fractures in athletes) with 8–20 week teriparatide courses, though formal RCT data for fracture repair remains limited. The synergy with BPC-157 and TB-500 in the compatibility matrix reflects the complementary mechanisms: teriparatide drives bone formation directly, while BPC-157 accelerates the vascular supply to the fracture callus and TB-500 promotes systemic cellular repair migration. The osteosarcoma risk from teriparatide requires precise framing. In the long-term carcinogenicity rat study that prompted the FDA black box warning, Fischer 344 rats treated with teriparatide at doses 3–60x the human equivalent for 2 years (essentially lifetime exposure) developed osteosarcomas at significant rates. Critically, this osteosarcoma signal has never been observed in approximately 2,800 patients across clinical trials or in over two decades of post-marketing surveillance data in millions of patient exposures. The mechanistic explanation is that Fischer 344 rats have physiologically active bone growth throughout their lifespan, while adult humans with closed growth plates do not maintain the same osteoblast proliferation dynamics. The 24-month lifetime maximum use limit exists because it was imposed by the FDA at the time of approval based on this rat data — not because osteosarcoma has been clinically documented in humans. Nonetheless, the contraindications derived from this concern (open growth plates, Paget's disease, skeletal radiation history, elevated alkaline phosphatase) are absolute and should be rigorously applied.

rows.notes: Clinical standard. Do not alter dose.

washout: Cycle Length: Varies based on bone scans.
Maximum lifetime cumulative use is strictly 24 months due to osteosarcoma risks in long-term models.
contraindications: Paget's disease of bone — the abnormal, accelerated bone turnover that characterizes Paget's disease creates unpredictable and potentially excessive osteoblast responses to PTH1R stimulation; absolute contraindication.

Prior radiation therapy to the skeleton — radiotherapy permanently alters bone cell biology and increases the theoretical risk of radiation-induced sarcoma development in cells stimulated by PTH1R activation; absolute contraindication per FDA label.

Open growth plates in pediatric subjects — teriparatide stimulates osteoblast proliferation at endosteal and periosteal surfaces; in subjects with active growth plates, uncontrolled stimulation of growth plate osteoprogenitor cells carries developmental and theoretical sarcoma risk.

Unexplained elevated serum alkaline phosphatase — high ALP indicates abnormal bone turnover that may reflect undiagnosed Paget's, malignancy, or other bone disease; requires investigation before teriparatide initiation.
History of primary malignancy with skeletal metastases or high risk of skeletal metastasis — PTH1R stimulation in bone with metastatic lesions may accelerate lesion growth; contraindicated.

Pre-existing hypercalcemia — teriparatide increases serum calcium via both increased bone resorption (transient) and increased renal calcium reabsorption; in subjects already hypercalcemic, further calcium elevation risks cardiac arrhythmia, nephrocalcinosis, and soft tissue calcification.
Primary hyperparathyroidism — endogenous PTH is already elevated; the mechanism mimics the continuous PTH exposure that drives bone resorption rather than formation.
Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min) — teriparatide has not been adequately studied in subjects with severe renal failure; calcium/phosphate dysregulation risk is amplified.

Concurrent bisphosphonate therapy — bisphosphonates inhibit the osteoclast activity that PTH requires to prime osteoblast formation signaling; co-administration significantly blunts teriparatide efficacy; sequential therapy (bisphosphonate after teriparatide is discontinued) is the preferred strategy.
Pregnancy — PTH1R signaling has roles in fetal skeletal development; safety not established; avoid.
Breastfeeding — not recommended; safety data insufficient.

Prior teriparatide or abaloparatide treatment completing 24-month cumulative lifetime exposure — the 24-month maximum is a lifetime cap, not a per-cycle cap; exceeded use carries the osteosarcoma risk on which the FDA boxed warning is based.
Known hypersensitivity to teriparatide or any formulation excipients including metacresol (the preservative used in multidose pens).
sideEffects: Hypercalcemia — the most pharmacologically expected adverse effect; teriparatide transiently elevates serum calcium through bone resorption activation and renal reabsorption; symptoms include nausea, weakness, constipation, confusion, and cardiac arrhythmia at severe levels; occurs most commonly in the first months; serum calcium should be monitored 1 month after initiation.
Hypercalciuria — elevated urinary calcium excretion parallel to hypercalcemia; important to monitor in subjects with a history of nephrolithiasis.
Nausea — one of the most commonly reported adverse effects in clinical trials; onset often within 1–2 hours of injection; related to the acute PTH pulse.
Dizziness and orthostatic hypotension — particularly in the hour following injection; injecting while sitting or lying down reduces risk.
Leg cramps — most frequent musculoskeletal adverse effect in clinical trials; lower extremity muscle cramping within hours of dosing.
Headache — commonly reported in clinical trial data; transient.
Joint aches and arthralgia — reported in a subset of subjects; related to calcium flux and bone remodeling activity.
Fatigue — general; particularly in early treatment weeks as the PTH signaling establishes new bone remodeling dynamics.
Injection site reactions — pain, redness, swelling, and bruising at the subcutaneous injection site; typically mild and self-limiting.
Elevated serum uric acid — reported in clinical trials; mechanism not fully characterized; may be relevant in subjects with gout or hyperuricemia.

Osteosarcoma (theoretical in humans) — carries a black box FDA warning based on rat carcinogenicity studies at supraphysiologic lifetime doses; no confirmed osteosarcoma cases attributed to teriparatide have been documented in human clinical use across over two decades of post-marketing surveillance.
Elevated alkaline phosphatase — expected pharmacological response to osteoblast activation; not an adverse event per se but a monitored laboratory marker.
Tachycardia — transient; related to acute PTH pulse and calcium flux; reported in some subjects within minutes of injection.

records.name: Tesamorelin
records.description: Tesamorelin is a GHRH analog consisting of the full 44 amino acids of endogenous GHRH with a trans-3-hexenoic acid group attached to the N-terminus — a modification that protects it from enzymatic degradation and extends its biological half-life while preserving the complete native GHRH receptor binding architecture. Unlike CJC-1295 No DAC (which is derived from the first 29 amino acids of GHRH), tesamorelin uses the entire GHRH sequence, making its receptor activation more faithful to the natural hormone and producing potent GH and IGF-1 responses. It is FDA-approved under the brand name Egrifta specifically for the treatment of HIV-associated lipodystrophy — a metabolic condition characterized by visceral fat accumulation caused by antiretroviral therapy — making it one of the very few GHRH analogs to have completed the full FDA approval pathway. The defining clinical characteristic of tesamorelin is its specificity for visceral adipose tissue (VAT) reduction. Where most GHRH analogs produce general body composition improvements, tesamorelin has been consistently demonstrated in multiple FDA pivotal trials to reduce visceral fat by 15–20% over 6-month protocols, with parallel improvements in triglycerides, non-HDL cholesterol, and markers of cardiovascular risk. The mechanism is GH-driven lipolysis specifically in visceral fat depots — tesamorelin's potent IGF-1 elevation combined with the GH pulse directs lipid mobilization preferentially from the visceral compartment. This has made it the compound of choice in research protocols targeting abdominal fat specifically, particularly for subjects with metabolic syndrome, insulin-treated diabetes, or HIV lipodystrophy. It also shows cognitive benefits — trials have documented improvements in cognition and executive function in older adults with mild cognitive impairment. Compared to CJC-1295 No DAC and sermorelin, tesamorelin is the most potent GHRH analog in this database and carries the strongest clinical evidence base. The trade-off is a more demanding side effect profile: injection site erythema (redness and irritation) is more common with tesamorelin than other GHRH analogs, likely due to the N-terminal fatty acid modification. Glucose metabolism effects are also more clinically significant — meaningful transient blood sugar elevations occur in a subset of subjects, and fasting discipline around injection time is important. It is contraindicated alongside CJC-1295 (both DAC and No DAC), sermorelin, and HGH 191aa due to direct GHRH receptor redundancy.

rows.notes: Typically administered right before bed on an empty stomach.
Administered morning (fasted) and pre-bed (fasted).

washout: Cycle Length: 8 to 12 weeks.
Washout: 4-8 weeks off.
contraindications: Active malignancy of any type — GH and IGF-1 elevation accelerates tumor cell proliferation.
History of malignancy — exercise caution; tesamorelin should not be initiated without careful oncology risk assessment.
Disruption of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis — pituitary tumors, pituitary surgery, head trauma, cranial radiation, or hypopituitarism from any cause.
Concurrent use with CJC-1295 No DAC, CJC-1295 DAC, sermorelin, or HGH 191aa — direct GHRH receptor redundancy and additive GH/IGF-1 overstimulation.
Concomitant glucocorticoid therapy — inhibits GH secretion and IGF-1 production.
Uncontrolled diabetes mellitus or significant insulin resistance — tesamorelin produces the most pronounced blood glucose effects of the GHRH analogs in this database.
Diabetic ketoacidosis.
Known hypersensitivity to tesamorelin, mannitol (excipient), or any formulation components.
Pregnancy — teratogenicity not established; avoid.
Breastfeeding — safety not established; avoid.
Pediatric use with open growth plates — risk of disproportionate bone growth stimulation.
Severe carpal tunnel syndrome — GH-mediated fluid retention worsens nerve compression.
Active proliferative or severe non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy — IGF-1 elevation may worsen retinal vasculopathy.
sideEffects: Injection site erythema (redness) — most distinctive adverse effect of tesamorelin vs. other GHRH analogs; more frequent and pronounced than with CJC-1295 or sermorelin; reported in approximately 6.4–25% of subjects in FDA trial data.
Injection site pain and irritation — discomfort at administration site; rotate sites to minimize.
Water retention and peripheral edema — GH-mediated sodium and fluid retention; more prominent in the first 4 weeks.
Joint pain and arthralgia — GH-related periarticular fluid accumulation; common.
Joint stiffness — particularly wrists, hands, and knees.
Myalgia (muscle pain) — GH-mediated; typically transient.
Tingling or numbness in extremities — paresthesia from GH-related fluid shifts.
Carpal tunnel syndrome — GH-mediated median nerve compression; more likely at higher doses and in predisposed subjects.
Mild to moderate blood sugar elevations — transient fasting glucose increases; monitor glycemic status throughout.
Nausea — reported in phase 3 data.
Vomiting — less common.
Headache — vasodilation-related; transient.
Fatigue — early-cycle adaptation.
Dizziness.
Elevated IGF-1 — supraphysiologic IGF-1 levels possible at higher doses; monitor with blood work on extended cycles.
Hypersensitivity reactions — urticaria, rash, pruritus, flushing; more commonly reported than with other GHRH analogs; likely related to the trans-3-hexenoic acid modification.
Anaphylaxis — rare but documented.
Injection site antibody formation — anti-tesamorelin antibodies develop in some subjects with prolonged use; may reduce efficacy.
Pituitary downregulation — risk with cycles beyond 12 weeks without washout.

records.name: Tesofensine
records.description: Tesofensine is a triple monoamine reuptake inhibitor — meaning it simultaneously blocks the reuptake transporters for serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine (hence SNDRI: serotonin-noradrenaline-dopamine reuptake inhibitor). What that means in plain terms: when you eat, your brain releases these three neurotransmitters to signal satisfaction and reduce the urge to keep eating. Normally they are rapidly cleared by reuptake transporters. Tesofensine blocks those transporters, so serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine all remain elevated and active for longer — producing a powerful, sustained suppression of appetite, a meaningful reduction in food-seeking behavior driven by dopaminergic pathways, and an increase in resting energy expenditure driven by the norepinephrine component. It also silences GABAergic neurons in the lateral hypothalamus — a feeding-control center in the brain — which independently reduces eating behavior. Uniquely, it indirectly amplifies cholinergic transmission and raises BDNF levels, giving it mild cognitive and potentially antidepressant properties beyond its weight management profile. The Phase 2 clinical data from the Lancet-published TIPO-1 trial is striking. At 0.5mg daily over 24 weeks, tesofensine produced 9.2% mean weight loss versus 2.0% for placebo — approximately double the weight loss seen with sibutramine or rimonabant, the best-performing approved agents at the time. At 1.0mg it pushed to 10.6%. This made it the most potent oral weight loss compound documented at the time of the trial. It achieves these results through an entirely CNS-mediated mechanism — it does not touch GLP-1, GIP, amylin, or any metabolic receptor that the injectable compounds in this database target, making it genuinely complementary rather than redundant when stacked with any incretin-based protocol. The synergy with semaglutide and retatrutide is particularly notable: semaglutide suppresses appetite peripherally and via brainstem GLP-1 receptors, while tesofensine suppresses appetite centrally via monoaminergic pathways — two completely different hunger circuits firing simultaneously. What makes tesofensine uniquely challenging to use responsibly is its pharmacokinetics. Its half-life is approximately 9 days — far longer than any other compound in this database — meaning the drug accumulates in the body over multiple weeks of daily dosing before reaching steady state, and after stopping, effects persist for weeks before clearing. This makes traditional dose titration logic more complex: you are not adjusting a daily peak but a slowly rising systemic level. Early morning dosing is non-negotiable — dosing even in the afternoon will result in residual CNS stimulation interfering with sleep architecture. This same property is why the every-other-day protocol exists: for CNS-sensitive researchers, EOD at 250mcg prevents excessive accumulation while still maintaining therapeutically relevant steady-state levels.

rows.notes: Assess central nervous system tolerance.
Standard therapeutic dose. Do not exceed.
Because the half-life is ~9 days, dosing EOD prevents excessive CNS accumulation and insomnia in sensitive researchers.

washout: Cycle Length: Maximum cycle length is 6 months.
Washout: Extremely long half-life (~9 days). Effects will persist for weeks after abrupt cessation.
contraindications: Current or recent use of MAOIs (monoamine oxidase inhibitors) — concurrent use risks life-threatening serotonin syndrome; require minimum 14-day washout after MAOI discontinuation before starting.
Current use of SSRIs or SNRIs — additive serotonergic load significantly raises serotonin syndrome risk; coordinate carefully with prescribing physician.
Current use of other stimulant compounds or sympathomimetics (amphetamines, phentermine, pseudoephedrine) — additive cardiovascular and CNS stimulant effects.
Uncontrolled hypertension — norepinephrine reuptake inhibition raises heart rate and may elevate blood pressure; baseline cardiovascular assessment recommended.
Pre-existing cardiac arrhythmias or tachycardia — heart rate increases of 7.4 BPM at the 0.5mg dose were observed in Phase 2 data.
History of anxiety disorders, panic disorder, or generalized anxiety disorder — norepinephrine/dopamine elevation significantly worsens anxiety and jitteriness.
History of bipolar disorder or manic episodes — dopamine elevation may precipitate manic episodes.
History of psychosis or schizophrenia spectrum disorders — dopaminergic potentiation may exacerbate psychotic symptoms.
History of substance use disorder, particularly stimulant abuse — dopamine transporter inhibition creates some abuse potential in predisposed individuals.
History of suicidal ideation — monitor closely; mood changes including depressed mood reported in Phase 2 data.
Pregnancy — CNS stimulant activity; safety not established; avoid use.
Breastfeeding — safety not established; avoid use.
Known hypersensitivity to tesofensine or any formulation excipients.
Severe hepatic impairment — metabolized hepatically; clearance impaired.
Severe renal impairment — limited safety data.
Concomitant use with triptans — serotonergic interaction risk.
Concomitant use with tramadol or other serotonergic opioids — additive serotonin syndrome risk.
Pediatric use — safety and efficacy not established.
sideEffects: Insomnia — most clinically problematic adverse effect; the ~9-day half-life means CNS stimulation is persistent; strict early morning dosing is mandatory to minimize this.
Dry mouth — reported frequently across all dose levels in Phase 2 trials; driven by noradrenergic and cholinergic modulation.
Elevated resting heart rate — mean increase of 7.4 BPM at 0.5mg dose in Phase 2 data; consistent across subjects; dose-dependent.
Nausea — reported across dose groups; generally mild and transient.
Constipation and hard stools — gastrointestinal motility effects of monoamine modulation.
Diarrhea — paradoxically reported in some subjects alongside constipation; inconsistent GI motility effects.
Anxiety and jitteriness — norepinephrine and dopamine elevation amplify anxiety in predisposed subjects.
Elevated blood pressure — modest increases observed at higher doses; monitor in subjects with borderline hypertension.
Headache — common during the early accumulation phase as CNS monoamine levels climb toward steady state.
Depressed mood — observed in Phase 2 extension data; may reflect appetite satiety appetite center desensitization over time or dopamine dysregulation.

Loss of appetite suppression over time — Phase 2 appetite data showed the composite satiety score diminished after week 12 despite continued weight loss; appetite suppression partially attenuates with sustained use.
CNS accumulation effects from long half-life — gradual buildup over 4–6 weeks of daily dosing may produce intensifying side effects not apparent in the first 1–2 weeks.
Flatulence — reported in Phase 2 data.
Dizziness.
Tremor or fine motor jitteriness — norepinephrine-mediated at higher doses.
Reduced libido or sexual dysfunction — serotonergic effects comparable to SSRI class.

Withdrawal effects upon cessation — due to long half-life, abrupt discontinuation may produce extended low-grade withdrawal: fatigue, mood changes, increased appetite; gradual tapering is recommended.
Potential abuse liability in predisposed individuals — dopamine transporter inhibition; lower risk than classical stimulants but not zero in individuals with stimulant use history.

records.name: Testagen
records.description: Testagen is a synthetic tetrapeptide (Lys-Glu-Asp-Gly) Khavinson bioregulator derived from testicular tissue polypeptide extracts — identified as the bioactive core sequence responsible for the Leydig cell regulatory, testosterone synthesis-supporting, and testicular tissue-normalizing activity of the native testicular extract. The testes perform two biologically distinct and equally essential functions: endocrine secretion (testosterone production by Leydig cells in the testicular interstitium, regulated by LH from the anterior pituitary) and spermatogenesis (production of mature spermatozoa by the seminiferous tubule system, involving Sertoli cells and regulated by both FSH and intratesticular testosterone). Both functions decline with aging — a process termed andropause or late-onset hypogonadism in the clinical literature — characterized by: age-related Leydig cell loss and reduced Leydig cell steroidogenic enzyme activity, declining testosterone production beginning in the third decade and accelerating after 50, reduced testicular volume, diminished sperm production quality (reduced motility, increased morphological abnormalities, elevated DNA fragmentation), and Sertoli cell functional decline with aging. Testagen acts as a bioregulator at the testicular cell level — interacting with Leydig cell and Sertoli cell surface receptors and transcription factors to normalize the gene expression programs governing steroidogenesis (StAR protein, CYP11A1, 3β-HSD, 17β-HSD enzyme expression), LH receptor sensitivity, intratesticular testosterone maintenance, and the cellular support functions of Sertoli cells for spermatogenesis. Unlike HCG (which pharmacologically forces Leydig cell activation through exogenous LH receptor stimulation), Testagen works through the endogenous bioregulator mechanism — normalizing the quality and responsiveness of the Leydig cell's own steroidogenic machinery rather than overriding it with exogenous gonadotropin stimulation. The mechanistic distinction between Testagen and the HPG axis pharmacological compounds in Category VII (kisspeptin, gonadorelin, HCG, HMG) is fundamental and explains why Testagen occupies a different therapeutic role in male hormone optimization. Category VII compounds work through the hormonal signaling cascade: kisspeptin activates hypothalamic GnRH neurons, gonadorelin delivers the GnRH pulse to the pituitary, HCG mimics LH at the Leydig cell receptor, HMG provides both LH and FSH signals. All of these are pharmacological signal amplification approaches — they deliver or amplify the hormonal message that tells the testes to produce testosterone. Testagen works differently: it acts at the testicular tissue level as a bioregulator that normalizes the Leydig cell's intrinsic capacity to respond to the LH signal it already receives. A Leydig cell with diminished steroidogenic enzyme expression, reduced mitochondrial function, and accumulated oxidative damage produces suboptimal testosterone even when adequately stimulated by LH — Testagen addresses this steroidogenic machinery quality problem rather than the LH signal strength problem. This makes Testagen uniquely complementary to HCG (signal + machinery quality) and kisspeptin (upstream signal normalization + downstream machinery quality). The synergy with Prostamax represents the complete male reproductive system bioregulator approach: Testagen normalizes testicular function and testosterone production quality; Prostamax normalizes prostatic tissue response to that testosterone. Together they address both the testosterone-producing organ (testes) and the primary testosterone-responding organ (prostate) simultaneously — a paired intervention that no single compound in the database addresses alone. The 16-week gradual titration protocol represents the most conservative introduction appropriate for subjects with significantly compromised testicular function where gradual bioregulator-driven restoration is preferred over the rapid stimulation of the standard 10-day protocol. Subjects on TRT who wish to use Testagen to maintain testicular function and steroidogenic enzyme quality during suppression should note that the HCG-free window (if any) in their TRT protocol is the optimal Testagen administration window, as some endogenous LH signaling is required for Testagen's normalized Leydig cell steroidogenic program to produce meaningful testosterone output.

rows.notes: Standard Khavinson protocol. Repeat every 6 months.

protocols.label: Alternative Titration 4: TRT Testicular Maintenance Protocol (Goal — preserve Leydig cell steroidogenic enzyme quality and testicular volume during testosterone replacement therapy; for TRT subjects not using HCG)

rows.notes: Quarterly maintenance cycles while on TRT. Preserves Leydig cell mitochondrial function and steroidogenic enzyme expression quality during the LH suppression of TRT. Does not restore testosterone production in the context of full LH suppression — maintains Leydig cell health for future restoration.

protocols.label: Alternative Titration 5: Prostamax + Testagen Complete Androgen Axis Protocol (Goal — simultaneous testicular testosterone production quality (Testagen) + prostatic androgen response normalization (Prostamax) for comprehensive male reproductive aging intervention)

washout: Standard Protocol — Repeat every 6 months.
Extended Protocol — 20-day cycle. Repeat every 4-6 months.
16-Week Conservative Protocol — 16-week cycle followed by 8-week washout. Repeat as indicated by Total T labs.
Male Fertility Protocol — 30-day cycle. Allow 90 days before reassessing sperm analysis.
TRT Maintenance Protocol — 10-day cycle every 3 months while on TRT.
Complete Androgen Axis Protocol — 10-day concurrent cycle. Repeat every 4-6 months.
contraindications: Testicular cancer — Testagen's Leydig cell and testicular tissue gene program normalization in the context of testicular malignancy (germ cell tumors, Leydig cell tumors, Sertoli cell tumors) is contraindicated; direct testicular bioregulator activity in malignant testicular tissue requires oncological evaluation.

Hormone-dependent prostate cancer — Testagen's normalization of testosterone production quality and Leydig cell steroidogenic capacity provides the androgen substrate that fuels androgen receptor-expressing prostate cancer cells; absolute contraindication shared with all compounds that restore or amplify testosterone production.

Active androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) — Testagen's mechanism directly opposes the therapeutic intent of GnRH agonist/antagonist or anti-androgen therapy used for prostate cancer or other testosterone suppression indications.

Klinefelter syndrome with severe primary testicular failure — in subjects with severely damaged testicular tissue and absent Leydig cell function, Testagen requires viable target cells to produce its bioregulator effect; in subjects with functionally absent Leydig cells, efficacy is reduced and hormonal expectations should be calibrated accordingly.
Known hypersensitivity to Testagen (Lys-Glu-Asp-Gly tetrapeptide) or formulation excipients.

Concurrent exogenous testosterone therapy at supraphysiological doses without HCG co-administration — exogenous testosterone at high doses suppresses pituitary LH secretion; in the context of complete LH suppression, Testagen's Leydig cell gene program normalization cannot be translated into meaningful testosterone production as the LH activation signal is absent.
Pediatric use prior to established puberty — testicular bioregulator activity during prepubertal testicular development has not been characterized.
Female subjects — Testagen is a testes-specific bioregulator with no established tissue target, mechanism, or indication in female biology.
sideEffects: Mild testosterone elevation — the expected and desired pharmacological effect; gradual improvement in serum testosterone as Leydig cell steroidogenic machinery quality normalizes over cycle weeks; physiological normalization rather than supraphysiological supplementation levels.

Mild testicular ache or sensitivity — as Leydig cell and Sertoli cell activity increases in response to bioregulator stimulation, the testes experience increased metabolic activity and blood flow; mild testicular discomfort is commonly reported in the first 1–2 weeks; benign and transient.

Mild increase in libido — associated with the gradual testosterone normalization; typically experienced as a desired effect; can be an overstimulation in subjects who are sensitive to androgen fluctuation.
Mild acne or skin oiliness — as androgen levels normalize upward, sebaceous gland activity may increase mildly in some subjects; typically minor and self-limiting.
Mild mood improvement and increased assertiveness — androgen normalization effects on the CNS; typically within normal range and experienced as positive by most subjects.
Injection site mild reaction — standard subcutaneous peptide response.

No serious androgenic adverse events documented in the Khavinson research literature — Testagen's testosterone-normalizing mechanism produces physiological rather than supraphysiological androgen restoration; the serious adverse effects of exogenous androgens (erythrocytosis, cardiovascular risk amplification, severe HPG axis suppression) are not associated with the bioregulator mechanism.
Unknown interaction profile with modern TRT protocols — formal pharmacokinetic interaction data between Testagen and exogenous testosterone formulations does not exist.

records.name: Thymalin
records.description: Thymalin is a natural polypeptide bioregulator extracted from the thymic tissue of young calves through a proprietary aqueous extraction process developed by the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology — the same research group responsible for the Khavinson bioregulator system. Unlike the synthetic dipeptide and tetrapeptide Khavinson bioregulators (Vilon, Epithalon, Pinealon), Thymalin is a heterogeneous mixture of naturally occurring thymic peptides rather than a single defined sequence — making it analogous to Cerebrolysin in the neural space: a complex biological extract delivering multiple synergistic peptide signals rather than a single molecular entity. The core active components of Thymalin include thymosin alpha-1 precursor fragments, thymulin, thymopoietin fragments, and other thymus-derived immunoregulatory peptides. Together these components act on the thymus gland itself to restore thymic architecture and function — a critical consideration given that the thymus undergoes progressive involution beginning in early adulthood, losing approximately 3% of its functional tissue per year and reaching minimal functional capacity by age 60–70. This thymic involution is a root cause of immunosenescence — the age-related decline of T-cell diversity, naive T-cell output, and immune surveillance that underlies the increased cancer incidence, chronic infection susceptibility, and vaccine non-response characteristic of aging. Thymalin acts at the level of the thymic microenvironment to support thymic epithelial cell function, restore cortical and medullary thymic architecture, and increase the output of naive T-cells into the peripheral circulation. The clinical research on Thymalin is predominantly from the Russian gerontological literature, spanning over four decades of application in the Soviet and post-Soviet medical system. Khavinson and colleagues published extensive data showing that Thymalin administration in elderly subjects (10mg/day for 10 consecutive days, repeated twice yearly) produced measurable improvements in T-lymphocyte subpopulation ratios, natural killer cell activity, immunoglobulin synthesis, and delayed-type hypersensitivity responses — all markers of restored immune competence. In longitudinal studies following elderly subjects over 6–8 years, subjects receiving twice-yearly Thymalin plus Epithalon showed dramatically reduced all-cause mortality compared to age-matched controls, reduced cardiovascular events, reduced cancer incidence, and reduced infectious disease frequency. While the methodological limitations of these studies (single-center, predominantly Russian, limited blinding) preclude definitive conclusions, the consistency of the findings across multiple cohorts and the biological plausibility of thymic restoration as an anti-aging intervention make Thymalin one of the most compelling longevity compounds in this database. The combination with Epithalon specifically addresses complementary aging clocks: Thymalin restores immune system age while Epithalon addresses telomeric/epigenetic age — providing a dual-axis anti-aging intervention that neither compound achieves alone. The 10-day consecutive protocol and twice-yearly administration schedule are not arbitrary — they reflect the pharmacodynamic duration of thymic restoration from a single Thymalin course. The 10-day loading period saturates thymic tissue with bioregulator peptides and triggers a restorative cascade in thymic epithelial cells that persists for months after the course ends, as newly educated T-cells are progressively released into the periphery and establish immune memory. Running Thymalin continuously would not add incremental benefit once the thymic restoration cycle is established, and may produce desensitization of the regulatory pathways that make the pulsatile protocol effective. The 6-month inter-cycle interval aligns with the estimated duration of the thymic restoration benefit before re-stimulation is required to maintain elevated immune competence.

rows.notes: Standard Russian clinical protocol. 10 consecutive days. Can be administered at any time of day. Repeat every 6 months.

records.name: Thymosin Alpha-1
records.description: Thymosin Alpha-1 (Tα1) is a 28-amino acid peptide originally isolated from thymosin Fraction 5 of calf thymus gland by Allan Goldstein in the 1970s and subsequently synthesized as thymalfasin — the form now approved in over 35 countries for the treatment of hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and as an immune adjuvant in cancer therapy and vaccine non-responders. Endogenous Tα1 is produced by thymic epithelial cells and serves as the thymus gland's primary peptide signal for educating and activating T-lymphocytes. Its mechanism centers on MHC-I (Major Histocompatibility Complex Class I) upregulation — Tα1 increases MHC-I expression on antigen-presenting cells and tumor cells, making them more visible to cytotoxic T-lymphocytes (CD8+ T cells) that would otherwise fail to recognize and eliminate them. Beyond MHC-I upregulation, Tα1 activates Toll-like receptors 2 and 9 on dendritic cells, driving dendritic cell maturation and the initiation of adaptive immune responses. It simultaneously promotes Th1 cytokine polarization (IL-2, IFN-γ, TNF-α) — the cellular immune arm responsible for fighting intracellular pathogens, viruses, and cancer — while suppressing the Th2-dominant patterns associated with allergic and chronic inflammatory states. Tα1 also activates NK (Natural Killer) cells directly, providing an innate immune boost independent of adaptive T-cell priming. The clinical evidence for Thymosin Alpha-1 is among the strongest of any peptide in this database. In hepatitis B and C, randomized controlled trials demonstrated significantly improved sustained virological response rates when Tα1 was added to standard antiviral therapy — the mechanism being Tα1's restoration of the exhausted anti-viral T-cell response characteristic of chronic viral infection. In cancer, Tα1 improves response rates to checkpoint inhibitor therapy and conventional chemotherapy by restoring immune surveillance in the tumor microenvironment. In vaccine non-responders — particularly immunocompromised patients (HIV, end-stage renal disease, elderly) who fail to mount adequate antibody responses to influenza, hepatitis B, or SARS-CoV-2 vaccines — Tα1 administered peri-vaccination significantly improves seroconversion rates. The COVID-19 pandemic generated extensive clinical data on Tα1 in severe disease: multiple Chinese clinical trials demonstrated reduced mortality, reduced ICU admission rates, and faster lymphocyte count recovery when Tα1 was administered to critically ill COVID-19 patients with lymphopenia. This clinical record makes Thymosin Alpha-1 the most evidence-supported immune-activating peptide in Category VI. The immune activation mechanism that makes Tα1 therapeutically powerful also defines its primary contraindication framework. Organ transplant recipients depend on pharmacological immunosuppression to prevent rejection of the transplanted organ; Tα1's restoration and amplification of T-cell function, MHC-I upregulation, and Th1 cytokine production directly counteracts this immunosuppression and creates acute rejection risk. This contraindication is absolute. Autoimmune disorders present a more nuanced picture: Tα1's immunomodulatory activity is often described as "normalizing" rather than simply "stimulating" — it restores appropriate immune regulation rather than uniformly amplifying all immune activity. In Hashimoto's thyroiditis, some case series suggest Tα1 may reduce inflammatory activity by restoring T-regulatory cell function. However, in conditions driven primarily by Th1 immune excess (rheumatoid arthritis, Type 1 diabetes, multiple sclerosis), Tα1's Th1-polarizing activity could theoretically worsen disease activity. The "use caution" designation for autoimmune conditions reflects this mechanistic uncertainty — the outcome depends heavily on the specific autoimmune disease and its immunological subtype.

records.name: Tirzepatide
records.description: Tirzepatide is the first dual incretin agonist — often called a "twincretin" — meaning it activates two separate hormone receptors at once: the GLP-1 receptor and the GIP receptor. If semaglutide is a single-key lock pick, tirzepatide picks two locks simultaneously. The GLP-1 side handles what you already know from semaglutide: appetite suppression, slower gastric emptying, and glucose-dependent insulin release. The GIP side adds something different — it acts directly on fat tissue to improve how the body stores and breaks down fat, enhances insulin sensitivity beyond what weight loss alone explains, and appears to amplify the appetite-suppressing effects of GLP-1 signaling in the brain. Critically, tirzepatide is deliberately engineered with stronger affinity for the GIP receptor than the GLP-1 receptor, which is intentional — it lets the compound push hard on the GIP side without triggering the severe nausea ceiling that limits aggressive GLP-1 dosing. The clinical results from the SURMOUNT trials reflect this dual mechanism directly. At the maximum 15mg weekly dose, subjects lost an average of 20–22% of total body weight — substantially exceeding the results seen with semaglutide at its maximum dose in head-to-head comparisons. In SURPASS-2, every tirzepatide dose outperformed semaglutide 1mg on both HbA1c reduction and weight loss. Beyond body composition, tirzepatide has demonstrated strong reductions in visceral fat specifically, improvements in triglycerides and HDL cholesterol, reductions in liver fat content (MASLD/NASH), and favorable cardiovascular outcomes data in the SURPASS-CVOT trial. It is also being actively studied for sleep apnea, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). What makes tirzepatide particularly notable from a tolerability standpoint is that GIP receptor activation does not carry the same nausea-inducing properties as GLP-1 receptor activation. This means the compound can achieve greater metabolic effect with a comparatively more manageable GI side effect profile than a pure GLP-1 agonist at equivalent efficacy levels. For researchers already familiar with semaglutide, tirzepatide represents the logical next step — higher ceiling, comparable weekly injection schedule, and an expanded mechanism that targets fat metabolism more directly. Its titration schedule starts at 2.5mg and steps up in 2.5mg increments, and — unlike semaglutide — skipping the initiation phase will almost certainly result in severe GI distress due to the higher baseline dose range.

records.name: VIP (Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide)
records.description: VIP (Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide) is an endogenous 28-amino acid neuropeptide that functions simultaneously as a neuromodulator, vasodilator, immunomodulator, and circadian regulator. It is found in the central nervous system (particularly the hypothalamic suprachiasmatic nucleus, the master circadian clock), the enteric nervous system, the respiratory tract, and throughout the immune system. VIP binds to two primary G protein-coupled receptors — VPAC1 and VPAC2 — which are expressed on smooth muscle, immune cells, epithelial cells, and neurons. Through VPAC receptor activation, VIP stimulates cAMP production, which drives smooth muscle relaxation (vasodilation and bronchodilation), upregulates T-regulatory cell differentiation, suppresses Th1/Th17 inflammatory cytokine production (TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-17), and promotes anti-inflammatory Th2 responses and IL-10 production. This immunomodulatory profile is profoundly relevant to chronic inflammatory conditions: VIP reduces the inflammatory burden without globally suppressing immune competence, positioning it as a sophisticated regulatory signal rather than an immunosuppressant. The most important clinical research application of VIP is in Chronic Inflammatory Response Syndrome (CIRS) — a multi-system inflammatory illness triggered by biotoxins from mold (primarily water-damaged buildings, Aspergillus, Stachybotrys), cyanobacteria, Lyme spirochetes, and other biofilm-producing organisms. In CIRS, endogenous VIP levels are consistently and markedly reduced, with low VIP serving as a diagnostic biomarker of the condition. In subjects with CIRS whose other inflammatory markers (MMP-9, TGF-β1, C4a, VEGF) have been normalized through prior stages of the Shoemaker Protocol, VIP administration — originally via intranasal route — has been documented to improve pulmonary artery systolic pressure (reduced from elevated levels toward normal), quality of life scores, cognitive symptoms, fatigue, and shortness of breath. The Shoemaker et al. prospective trial using intranasal VIP (50 mcg four times daily) demonstrated significant improvements in these parameters. VIP's role in circadian rhythm synchronization explains the morning/early afternoon dosing requirement: VIP is the primary neurotransmitter of the suprachiasmatic nucleus circadian clock and its dosing must align with the natural light-phase biological cycle to avoid circadian disruption. The vasodilatory properties of VIP are its most immediately apparent pharmacological activity and its most critical safety consideration. VIP is one of the most potent endogenous vasodilators known — acting on smooth muscle throughout the pulmonary, mesenteric, and systemic vasculature. This makes VIP exceptionally dangerous at high doses, rapid injection rates, or in subjects with baseline hypotension. The blood pressure drop can be sudden and significant, particularly within minutes of injection. The mandatory protocol note to "administer very slowly" is not precautionary language — it is the primary safety intervention for avoiding acute hypotensive episodes. Subjects must be seated or supine during administration and should not stand abruptly for at least 15–20 minutes post-injection. VIP should not be used until all upstream CIRS markers are normalized per the Shoemaker Protocol; using VIP prematurely in a subject with unresolved CIRS inflammatory drivers will produce only transient symptomatic benefit while the underlying inflammatory cycle continues.

records.name: Vitamin B12 (B1201)
records.description: Vitamin B12 (product code B1201) is a single-ingredient injectable delivering vitamin B12, typically as methylcobalamin, the active and readily usable form. It is a vitamin rather than a peptide, working as an essential cofactor in energy metabolism, nervous system function, and blood cell production, and it is given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. B12 is required for red blood cell formation, DNA synthesis, and the health of the myelin sheath that protects nerves, and it plays a central role in the methylation cycle that governs energy production and homocysteine clearance. Injectable delivery is valued because it bypasses the digestive absorption steps that many people, particularly older adults, vegetarians, and those with gut issues, struggle with. In practice, B1201 is used by people who want an energy, mood, and cognitive lift, or who need to correct a B12 deficiency that oral supplements are not adequately resolving. It is one of the most popular standalone injections because the effects of correcting low B12, including improved energy, clearer thinking, and better mood, can be noticeable and relatively quick. It appeals to vegetarians and vegans who lack dietary B12, older adults with reduced absorption, people on medications that deplete B12, and hard-training individuals who want metabolic and recovery support. It is typically administered in the morning as a standing weekly injection, and because B12 is water soluble and very well tolerated, it can be used consistently with a wide safety margin. Mechanistically, B12 acts as a cofactor for enzymes that produce red blood cells, synthesize DNA, maintain nerve myelin, and drive the methylation cycle that supports energy metabolism and homocysteine regulation. When B12 status is low, supplying it directly restores these processes and often produces a clear improvement in energy and cognition. Users should expect the most dramatic benefits when correcting an actual deficiency, with more subtle effects in those who are already replete. B12 is water soluble and excess is excreted, so toxicity is rare. Morning administration is preferred because B12 can be mildly energizing. Injection sites should be rotated, and anyone with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy should avoid high-dose B12, while those with kidney disease should use it under medical guidance.

rows.notes: Direct-dose vitamin B12 injection with no titration required. A typical protocol is 0.5 to 1 mL administered subcutaneously or intramuscularly 1 to 2 times per week, in the morning. Deficiency-correction protocols may use higher initial frequency under medical guidance. Rotate injection sites. Suitable for continuous use given the wide safety margin.

records.name: Vitamin D3 (D320)
records.description: Vitamin D3 (product code D320) is a single-ingredient injectable delivering cholecalciferol, the form of vitamin D the body produces in response to sunlight. It is a vitamin rather than a peptide, working as a hormone-like nutrient that regulates gene expression across many tissues, and it is given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Vitamin D3 is essential for calcium absorption and bone health, immune function, muscle strength, mood regulation, and healthy testosterone and hormone production. Injectable delivery is valued because it provides a reliable, high dose that bypasses the variability of oral absorption and is especially useful for people with low vitamin D status or absorption issues. In practice, D320 is used by people who want to correct or maintain healthy vitamin D levels, which is one of the most common nutrient insufficiencies, particularly in those with limited sun exposure, darker skin, or higher body fat that sequesters vitamin D. It appeals to users focused on immune resilience, bone and joint health, mood, and hormonal optimization, since adequate vitamin D supports all of these. Because vitamin D is fat soluble and stored in the body, it is dosed less frequently than the water-soluble B-vitamin blends, often weekly to monthly depending on status and the amount per dose. Users are strongly encouraged to base their dosing on bloodwork, since vitamin D can accumulate and both deficiency and excess carry risks. Mechanistically, vitamin D3 is converted in the liver and kidneys into its active hormone form, which binds the vitamin D receptor found throughout the body and influences calcium handling, immune signaling, muscle function, and hormone production. Because it is stored and can build up, monitoring blood levels is important to keep values in the healthy range and avoid toxicity. Users should expect gradual improvements in energy, mood, immune resilience, and lab values with consistent use, and should retest periodically. Injection sites should be rotated, and anyone with high blood calcium, kidney stones, sarcoidosis, or certain other conditions should use vitamin D only under medical supervision because these conditions raise the risk of vitamin D related complications.

rows.dose: 0.5 to 1 mL weekly to monthly, guided by bloodwork

records.name: Vladonix
records.description: Vladonix is a Khavinson cytomedin — peptide complex A-6 — extracted from the thymus gland tissue of young animals, developed as the oral thymic bioregulator of the Khavinson framework. The thymus is the organ responsible for producing and educating T-cells — the adaptive immune system's primary soldiers — and it progressively involutes (shrinks and loses function) beginning in adolescence, reaching near-total functional collapse by the sixth decade. Vladonix delivers a mixture of thymus-derived low-molecular-weight peptides that interact with thymic epithelial cells and thymocyte precursors, normalizing the gene expression programs governing T-cell maturation, thymic architecture maintenance, and the output of naive T-cells into peripheral circulation — effectively signaling the aging thymus to resume the productive T-cell education it has been progressively abandoning. Clinical research outcomes documented for Vladonix and predecessor thymic cytomedin preparations include normalization of CD4+/CD8+ T-cell ratios toward youthful ranges, increased numbers of circulating naive T-cells, improved T-cell proliferative response to stimulation, reduction in the accumulation of dysfunctional senescent T-cells, and documented 2-3x reductions in respiratory infection frequency in elderly subjects on regular Vladonix cycling. These outcomes are consistent with what thymopoietic restoration is expected to produce — a broader, more competent T-cell repertoire capable of responding to novel antigens, which translates clinically into fewer infections, better vaccine responses, and reduced susceptibility to cancer immune escape. What sets Vladonix apart from Vilon — the injectable synthetic dipeptide (Lys-Glu) thymic bioregulator also in this database — is not the target organ but the delivery depth and complexity. Vilon is a minimized two-amino-acid synthetic sequence delivering the defined thymopoietic core signal by injection; Vladonix is the full thymic tissue extract delivering the complete multi-peptide thymic signaling repertoire orally, including thymic hormonal components analogous to thymosin alpha-1, thymulin, and thymosin β4 that Vilon's stripped-down sequence does not replicate. Subjects on injectable Vilon can add Vladonix oral cycles to capture this broader thymic hormonal component; subjects preferring oral-only protocols use Vladonix as their complete thymic bioregulator.
